sections.label: Competitive economy and ageing population
sections.summary: The global economy is more competitive and digitalised, and Singapore has one of the fastest ageing populations, with one in four above 65 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The global economy is more competitive and digitalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We are one of the fastest ageing populations in the world with one in four Singaporeans above the age of 65 by 2030.

sections.label: Budget deficit and GST profiteering
sections.summary: It asks whether society provides stepping ladders, notes a third consecutive Budget deficit and reserves use, and raises concerns about businesses profiteering from the GST increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Do we leave individuals to find their own way, or do we as a society collectively agree to provide stepping ladders for those in need?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: That being said Mr Speaker, Sir, I do worry that this is our third consecutive year running a Budget deficit and we will be digging into our reserves yet again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: One of the concerns that has been echoed by residents is how do we prevent businesses profiteering from the GST increase at the expense of the consumers?

sections.label: Committee against Profiteering clarification
sections.summary: It seeks clarification from the Minister on how the Committee against Profiteering will be implemented and address concerns of businesses perceived to be profiteering from the GST increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Can I also seek clarification from the Minister on how the Committee against Profiteering will be implemented and how will it address concerns of businesses perceived to be profiteering from the GST increase?

sections.label: Digital capability and transformation funding
sections.summary: The Budget apportions $200 million for digital capability and polytechnic and ITE capacity, and an additional $100 million to support NTUC to scale up CTCs and new transformation grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In this Budget, we have apportioned significant resources such as $200 million for building digital capability and increasing the capacity at Polytechnics and ITE centres to engage in technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We will also invest in an additional $100 million to support NTUC to scale up CTCs and introduce new grants to support transformation plans.

sections.label: Scheme eligibility and payouts raised
sections.summary: The scheme's qualifying monthly income cap has been raised, age eligibility extended, and payouts increased especially for people with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The qualifying monthly income cap for this scheme has been raised, age eligibility has been extended and the payouts increased especially for people with disabilities.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model extension
sections.summary: The Progressive Wage Model will be extended to other industries and wage increases for low-wage workers will be co-funded under the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Progressive Wage Model will be extended to other industries and wage increases for low-wage workers will be co-funded under the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme.

sections.label: Budget aims and improvement areas
sections.summary: The Budget aims for a fair and inclusive Singapore, supports workers, businesses and households during the pandemic, and lists areas for improvement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: These programmes, among others, aim to ensure a fair and inclusive Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This Budget is a balanced budget, which provides support to workers, businesses and households to tackle the challenges due to the pandemic, and at the same time, it also prepares us for a more challenging future by transforming our businesses, developing new capabilities and investing in our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, several areas can be improved: The first is how the "Committee Against Profiteering" can prevent businesses from profiteering from the GST hike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Second, in light of future challenges, how do we remain relevant in the global economy and drive sector-specific industry transformation via the Industry Transformation Maps?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Third, we must continue our journey towards inclusive growth by providing assistance for platform workers, providing job opportunities for senior citizens who still wish to work and special needs workers and, and also address workplace discrimination through TAFEP legislation.

sections.label: HSA vaccine and test kit approval
sections.summary: HSA has not approved for public use any Singapore manufactured vaccine or Antigen Rapid Test kit for home use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the other hand, despite some initial hype, the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) has yet to approve for public use any Singapore manufactured vaccine or Antigen Rapid Test kit for home use, arguably two of the most critical resources needed in the pandemic.

sections.label: BioNTech manufacturing facility in Singapore
sections.summary: The Budget Statement highlighted that mRNA vaccine manufacturer BioNTech will establish a manufacturing facility in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On a related note, the Budget Statement highlighted that the mRNA vaccine manufacturer, BioNTech, will establish a manufacturing facility here.

sections.label: Singapore Global Innovation Index ranking
sections.summary: Singapore ranked eighth overall globally in the Global Innovation Index 2021 and has been in the top 10 for over a decade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Global Innovation Index 2021 published by the World Intellectual Property Office, Singapore ranked overall eighth globally, and has been in the top 10 list for more than a decade.

sections.label: South Korea overtakes Singapore ranking
sections.summary: In the 2021 ranking, South Korea rose to fifth position and overtook Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For the 2021 ranking, it is notable that South Korea shot to fifth position and overtook Singapore.

sections.label: GST hike household scenarios
sections.summary: Workers' Party colleagues explained why the GST hike is not necessary, citing four household scenarios in the Budget Statement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On GST, my Workers’ Party colleagues have explained why we do not think the GST hike is necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From paragraphs 286 to 287 of the Budget Statement, and also Annex F-3, there are four household scenarios highlighted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It will be noted that all the households comprise of a wedded couple living in an HDB flat, mostly with children; if the couple is of working age, the husband is always older and always earns more than the wife.

sections.label: Broader household illustrations requested
sections.summary: A speaker asks the Ministry to broaden its illustrations to include divorced families, families with a foreign spouse and adult singles living with elderly parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I wonder if the Ministry could, in future, be broader in its illustrations to capture some other types of households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Such other types of households, which are not uncommon, include divorced families, families with a foreign spouse and adult singles living with elderly parents.

sections.label: Wage rises versus cost increases
sections.summary: The passage states salary increases cannot fend off rising transport, food, household item and healthcare costs, with higher GST and carbon tax fuelling inflation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Salaries, if there had been any increases at all, are unable to fend off the rise in the cost of transport, cost of food, as well as other essential household items and healthcare services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And this Budget, we will see a higher GST next year, a higher carbon tax next year, which fuel inflation to an even higher level.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The combined effects of the trio – GST increase, carbon tax increase and wages increase – cannot be underestimated.

sections.label: Salaries versus headline inflation
sections.summary: Employees' salaries rose 3.3% in 2021 versus 3.6% in 2019, expected 3.5% in 2022, while Singapore's 2021 headline inflation was 3.9% to 4%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Employees' salaries went up by 3.3% in 2021 compared to 3.6% in 2019 and it is expected to rise by 3.5% in 2022, according to Mercer's 2021 Total Remuneration Survey (TRS).

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, Singapore's headline inflation in 2021 was 3.9% to 4%.

sections.label: GST offset package called temporary
sections.summary: Singaporeans note the Government's offset package cushions the GST rise but argue the package is only temporary.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While Singaporeans note that the Government has an offset package in place to cushion the effect of the GST rise, they argued that this offset package is only temporary.

sections.label: Residential property tax amounts and distribution
sections.summary: The passage asks the total annual residential property tax collected and its distribution by housing type, including GCB, landed, condominiums and HDB.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What is the total amount of property tax on residential property that the Government collects every year from this?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And what is the distribution of this property tax going by housing type, such as GCB, various landed properties, low and high-rise condominiums as well as HDB properties?

sections.label: Why sin taxes were not raised
sections.summary: The passage asks why sin taxes on gambling, alcohol and cigarettes were not increased in this Budget despite the need for revenue for an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Since the Government need to increase revenue to support the long-term needs of an ageing population, why were sin taxes, such as gambling, alcohol and cigarette taxes, not increased in this Budget?

sections.label: Solar panel energy limits
sections.summary: A solar panel on the whole island would still not generate enough energy for daily needs, raising whether carbon zero is realistic.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Even if we put a solar panel on the whole island, we will still not generate enough energy to meet our daily needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, my next question is: is it realistic for Singapore to aim for carbon zero?

sections.label: Tapping nuclear energy option
sections.summary: Singapore can prioritise reviewing nuclear energy as a clean energy option, with micro nuclear reactors enhancing safety, reliability and cost effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But the question is: how far are we from there?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I appreciate the response, that Singapore can give some priority to review the tapping of nuclear energy as part of our option to use clean energy, to meet our commitment to the global community on environmental sustainability, technological advances in micro nuclear reactors will enhance safety, reliability as well as cost effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We need to keep an open mind and tap this option in the future to enhance our energy security and resilience and reduce our dependence on other countries.

sections.label: Carbon tax raise clarification
sections.summary: The Government raised the carbon tax to international standards, with a target of $50 to $80 by 2030, and clarification was sought on extending it to smaller emitters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We recognise that the Government has finally thought it appropriate to raise the common tax to a level in line with international standards to help Singapore achieve a net-zero and emissions ambition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We support the move to see the common tax raise progressively to a target between $50 and $80 dollars by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: It will impose a temporary cause to Singaporeans, but we are of the view that when we do become a green economy, the impact of the carbon taxes will be reduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: However, I like to seek a clarification from the Minister on whether there are any efforts to extend the carbon tax to companies that emit less than 25,000 tonnes of GHGs per annum to enhance our efforts toward a net-zero ambition.

sections.label: Energy and chemicals industry data
sections.summary: The energy and chemicals industry contributed nearly 3% of GDP and employed about 28,000 people in 2017, with fuels and chemicals around 23% of merchandise trade in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: According to a 2019 answer by MTI to a Parliamentary Question (PQ), the energy and chemicals industry contributes nearly 3% of our GDP and employs about 28,000 people in 2017, with the majority in their 30s and 40s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In 2019, Singapore was the world's fourth biggest exporter of refined petroleum, and fuels and chemicals accounted for around 23% of our total merchandise trade, according to data from the World Bank and the Observatory of Economic Complexity.

sections.label: Electric vehicle charging points
sections.summary: Minister S Iswaran said there were around 2,200 EV charging points, with more than 600 to be deployed at public car parks in 2022 toward a 2030 target of 60,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Minister S Iswaran said that there were around 2,200 electric vehicle charging points in Singapore, of which, 300 were installed by commercial operators in the past year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In 2022, there will be more than 600 charging points deployed at public car parks under the joint LTA-URA pilot tender, in addition to charging points in other locations like private residences, malls and petrol stations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Minister also said that LTA will continue to monitor EV adoption trends and accelerate the deployment of our EV charging network where necessary to meet our 2030 target of 60,000 charging points island-wide.

sections.label: GST Voucher income threshold
sections.summary: Under the enhanced permanent GST Voucher Scheme, those with assessable income beyond $34,000 will not receive any assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: As for the enhancement to the permanent GST Voucher Scheme, those with an assessable income beyond $34,000 will not be receiving any assistance, a sharp cliff where, for some, these packages may no longer apply should they earn more.

sections.label: Resident population ageing statistics
sections.summary: Census 2020 figures show residents aged 65 and above rose to 15.2% in 2020 from 9% in 2010, with about one in four above 65 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: According to a Straits Times report on 27 July 2021, citing figures from Census 2020, residents aged 65 years and above form 15.2% of the resident population in 2020, up from 9% in 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: About one in four will be above 65 in 2030 and a corresponding increase in old-age dependency is to be expected.

sections.label: GST and healthcare costs
sections.summary: Subsidised public patients pay no GST, but GST on private clinics and non-structured hospitals is not absorbed, prompting a question on out-of-pocket healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While subsidised patients in public hospitals and polyclinics do not pay any GST, the GST on the goods and services provided by GST-registered private clinics and non-structured hospitals that Singaporeans do go to are not absorbed by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Can the Government assure Singaporeans that the hike in GST will not mean that Singaporeans are going to pay more in their out-of-pocket healthcare costs?

sections.label: Identifying families in crisis
sections.summary: The passage asks how the framework to identify families in crisis more quickly will be strengthened and welcomes ComLink's scaling to 21 towns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In English): Will the Government elaborate on how we will strengthen our framework to identify families in crisis more quickly?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I applaud the scaling up of the ComLink initiative nationwide to 21 towns.

sections.label: Youth mentorship access survey
sections.summary: A Young NTUC survey ranked mentorship second most useful for careers but little accessed, and about 1,200 youths joined virtual mentoring sessions in 2020 and 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the latest survey conducted by Young NTUC, youths and young adults ranked mentorship opportunities the second most useful in terms of career-related resources but they also noted that they have little access to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In 2020 and 2021, when physical events were curtailed, Young NTUC organised virtual career mentoring sessions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I understand that about 1,200 youths took part.

sections.label: Google Skills Ignition SG partnership
sections.summary: Google's Skills Ignition SG programme is a training partnership between Google, EDB, IMDA and SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: An excellent example of a multi-parties' involvement for training is Google's Skills Ignition SG programme, a partnership between Google, EDB, IMDA and SkillsFuture.

sections.label: Independent service providers' entitlements
sections.summary: As independent service providers, they are not employees and so are not entitled to employee rights such as sick leave, CPF contributions and medical expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As independent service providers, they are not employees and thus are not entitled to employee rights such as sick leave, mandatory leave, CPF contributions, medical expenses, so on and so forth.

sections.label: Self-employed workers and platform companies
sections.summary: In 2018, 8% to 10% of Singapore's resident workforce was self-employed, and the passage calls for reviewing their work conditions and amending legislation for platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As a gauge, consider in 2018, 8% to 10% of Singapore's resident workforce was self-employed or they did full-time independent work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is time for us to review their work conditions and consider if we should amend legislation to require platform companies to treat the full-time platform worker as employees as well as to allow them to form unions to protect their rights, including fair and timely payment.

sections.label: Singapore carbon tax
sections.summary: Singapore is the first or only Southeast Asian country to introduce a carbon tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Singapore is the first or the only Southeast Asian country to introduce a carbon tax.

sections.label: Motorcycle COE prices
sections.summary: In November 2021, an Adjournment Motion on motorcycle COEs was put forth, and MOT agreed high COE prices burden motorcycle owners, especially low-income segments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In November 2021, I put forth an Adjournment Motion on the ever-increasing issues of motorcycle COEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In responding to the Motion, MOT agreed on how the high COE prices burden motorcycle owners, especially those belonging to the low-income segments.

sections.label: Foreign spouses citizenship naturalisation
sections.summary: The Workers' Party called for foreign spouses to be given priority for citizenship naturalisation after five years on LTVP+, with three years of marriage and at least one child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On this issue, the Workers' Party has specifically called for foreign spouses to be given priority for citizenship naturalisation if they apply after five years on their LTVP+, on the condition that they have been married to their current Singaporean spouse for three years or more and they have at least one child together.

sections.label: Single parents subsidised flats
sections.summary: The Government allows single parents to buy subsidised flats without a development period and unwed single parents to buy up to a 3-room flat, but more flexibility is sought.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Although there are reform measures taken by the Government such as allowing single parents to buy subsidised flats without having to go through a development period and also allowing unwed single parents to purchase up to a 3-room flat in a non-mature estate from HDB or a resale flat, but I think more flexibility can be exercised to reduce the difficulties of this group.

sections.label: Stateless individuals in Singapore
sections.summary: As of end November 2020, there were 1,109 stateless individuals in Singapore, of which 76% have obtained Permanent Residence status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Minister for Home Affairs, as of end November 2020, there were 1,109 stateless individuals in Singapore, of which 76% have obtained Permanent Residence status.

sections.label: Core inflation rise
sections.summary: Core inflation rose 2.4% year-on-year last January, the highest in nine years, driven by food, electricity and gas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Just look at last January’s core inflation which has gone up by 2.4% on a year-on-year basis, reaching the highest level in nine years, driven by higher inflation in food, electricity and gas, as well as a smaller decline in the cost of retail and other goods.

sections.label: Malay households in rental flats
sections.summary: The Population Census showed Malay households in 1-room and 2-room rental flats more than doubled from about 9,100 in 2010 to 18,600 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Population Census showed that the number of Malay households living in 1-room and 2-room rental flats has more than doubled in 10 years, from around 9,100 in 2010 to 18,600 in 2020.

sections.label: Malay children aged 0 to 4
sections.summary: The 2020 Population Census recorded 38,668 Malay boys and girls aged 0 to 4 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to statistics from the 2020 Population Census, there were 38,668 Malay boys and girls aged 0 to 4 years old.

sections.label: Malay Language in preschools
sections.summary: 350 childcare centres provided Malay Language lessons this year out of more than 1,800 preschools, and PSLE Malay grades A* to C declined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The upbringing and teaching of Malay Language, whether at home or at childcare centres, are equally important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, I discovered from a reply by the Minister for Social and Family Development in April 2021 that 350 childcare centres provided Malay Language lessons beginning this year, despite having more than 1,800 preschools here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This means that only 19% of preschools here teach Malay Language.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moreover, the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) results showed a very clear indication that the percentage of Malay children who scored grade A* to C for the Malay Language had declined.

sections.label: Plans for Malay Language preschools
sections.summary: The passage asks what plans the Government has to increase preschools offering Malay Language teaching for the 38,668 children aged 0 to 4.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, what are the Government's plans to increase the number of preschools that can offer the teaching of Malay Language to meet the needs of the majority of the 38,668 children aged 0 to 4 years old, where currently only 350 preschools out of around 1,800 preschools that are doing so.

sections.label: Russia invades Ukraine
sections.summary: Russia invaded Ukraine on 24 February 2022, described as the biggest invasion of a European country since World War II.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Russia invaded Ukraine on 24 February 2022 in what has been described as the biggest invasion of a European country since World War II.

sections.label: Singapore sanctions on Russia
sections.summary: Singapore decided to follow suit and impose its own sanctions on Russia based on a principled approach to diplomacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Singapore decided to follow suit and impose its own sanctions on Russia based on our principled approach to diplomacy.

sections.label: Russia and Ukraine commodity prices
sections.summary: Russia and Ukraine are substantial commodity producers, and prices of oil, gas and agricultural commodities have spiked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Both Russia and Ukraine are substantial commodity producers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We have seen spikes in the prices of oil, gas and agricultural commodities.

sections.label: Polders and barrages plan
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee planned polders and barrages over 50 to 100 years to save Singapore from rising sea levels, costing at least $100 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Hon Members will recall Prime Minister Lee’s bold plan to build polders and barrages for a period of between 50 and 100 years to save Singapore from rising sea levels costing at least $100 billion.

sections.label: Tax increases and progressive policy
sections.summary: The Minister increased taxes on wealthier Singaporeans, and the progressive policy ensures low- and middle-income Singaporeans receive more benefits than paid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We must hold fast to our resolve to develop these strategic capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I now turn to the hon Minister’s decision to increase the tax responsibility on wealthier Singaporeans through personal income tax, property tax, luxury car tax and GST increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The progressive nature of our policy ensures that low- and middle-income Singaporeans will, on a net basis receive significantly more benefits from tax transfers than what they would have paid.

sections.label: Government spending share of GDP
sections.summary: Government spending excluding COVID-19 expenditure is 18% of GDP, the lowest among developed economies, yet produced better social and economic outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As the hon Minister mentioned, Government spending today, excluding COVID-19 related expenditure, stands at 18% of our GDP which is the lowest among developed economies but yet it has produced social and economic outcomes that have been better than most.

sections.label: Assurance Package landed property payout
sections.summary: The Assurance Package provides that a person owning a single private landed property with no income can get up to $1,600 over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Indeed, in the Assurance Package, it is provided that a person who owns a single private landed property but does not have income can get up to $1,600 over five years.

sections.label: Carbon credits and entrepreneurial talent
sections.summary: Speaker supports raising carbon tax and asks whether assistance can be given to entrepreneurial businesses with sustainability projects lacking scale for carbon credit financing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The final area I wish to touch on in my speech concerns the development of entrepreneurial talent undertaking sustainability initiatives that can generate carbon credits for use by businesses to offset carbon tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I support the move to increase the carbon tax as part of Singapore’s commitment to reduce emissions and tackle climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I note with interest that the hon Minister intends to allow businesses to use high quality, international carbon credits to offset up to 5% of their taxable incomes in lieu of paying carbon tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What I wish to explore is whether assistance may be provided to entrepreneurial businesses in Singapore which have promising sustainability projects but lack the scale necessary to attract carbon credit financing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: One suggestion I have is for Government or Statutory Boards to partner these businesses in the provision of services such as waste to energy plants to power lamp posts in business parks.

sections.label: Basic Retirement Sum increase
sections.summary: Speaker is concerned about raising the Basic Retirement Sum 3.5% yearly for five cohorts from 2023 to 2027, noting 435,000 aged 55 to 70 cannot meet the prevailing BRS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We must do all we can to increase the resilience of family units whatever form they might come in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am concerned about the plan to raise the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) by 3.5% per year for the next five cohorts turning 55 from 2023 to 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MOF said that eight in 10 CPF members turning 55 in 2027 will be able to set aside the heightened BRS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, some 435,000 Singaporeans aged between 55 and 70 are unable to meet the prevailing BRS.

sections.label: Children responsibility and net zero
sections.summary: Speaker says such occasions let children take responsibility for their actions and belongings, and welcomes the aim of net zero emissions by or around mid-century.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Occasions like these are opportunities for our children to take responsibility for their actions and their belongings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am glad to hear the Finance Minister announced that Singapore aims to achieve net zero emissions by or around mid-century.

sections.label: Workfare Income Supplement minimum income
sections.summary: The Finance Minister introduced a $500-a-month minimum income requirement for the Workfare Income Supplement from 2013, potentially affecting up to 46,600 employed residents earning under $500 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In his Budget Statement, the Finance Minister introduced a $500-a-month minimum income requirement to qualify for the Workfare Income Supplement from 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This could potentially impact up to 46,600 employed residents, inclusive of part-timers, who earn less than $500 a month.

sections.label: Minimum wage and Progressive Wage Model
sections.summary: Speaker welcomes requirements that local workers be paid at least $1,400 a month if companies employ foreign workers, and Government co-funding pay increases for low-wage workers over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We must ensure that every working Singaporean receives a decent minimum wage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I welcome the requirements for all local workers to be paid at least $1,400 a month, if their companies employ foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: All the workers are in a Progressive Wage Model (PWM) sector or occupation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am cheered that the Government is going to co-fund the pay increases for low-wage workers over the next five years.

sections.label: Civil servants and political masters
sections.summary: Civil servants should not second-guess what their political masters want or implement instructions blindly just because Ministers said so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Civil servants should not second-guess what their political masters want or implement instructions blindly, just because the Ministers said so.

sections.label: GST hike as last resort
sections.summary: Speaker believes a consumption tax hike should be a last resort, citing GST's regressiveness and Workers' Party alternative revenue levers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, it remains my belief that a consumption tax hike should be the last resort to increasing revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is because the GST is an inherently regressive tax, to which the poor pay a higher percentage of their income compared to the rich.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The GST Offset Package is meant to help lower-income households adjust but this will last only five to 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yesterday, Member of Parliament for Sengkang Assoc Prof Jamus Lim did a deep dive into the Workers' Party's alternative levers for raising revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This includes higher taxes in carbon emissions, multinational corporations and wealth, using a portion of land sales and increasing investment returns contribution, which can more than make up for shortfalls in revenue brought about by higher social spending without having to increase GST.

sections.label: Expenditure, deficit and GST hike
sections.summary: Total expenditure exceeded $100 billion with a projected $3 billion deficit, and a taskforce will tackle profiteering from the upcoming GST hike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Total Expenditure exceeded $100 billion, which is $4 billion higher than the Revised FY2021 estimate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The projected overall fiscal position for the year is a deficit of about $3 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Minister Lawrence Wong has explained its reasons and the fact that the GST increase will be done in stages and will only take place from next year onwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While it is unclear if this is due to an expectation of GST increase or other factors like the rise in the costs of energy and supplies, I welcome the establishment of a Taskforce by the Government to tackle profiteering and those who take advantage of the upcoming GST hike as an excuse to raise prices.

sections.label: SINGA borrowing financial impact
sections.summary: SINGA allows Government borrowings for major infrastructure lasting at least 50 years, and the Minister is asked to illustrate its financial impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One example is the Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act (SINGA) which allows Government borrowings for major national infrastructure projects that will last for at least 50 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If I may clarify, can Minister illustrate how significant the financial impact of SINGA has been on this year’s and future Budgets in an easy to read and digestible manner?

sections.label: LBC replaces previous development charges
sections.summary: Under the new Act, the LBC replaces Development Charge, Temporary Development Levy and Differential Premium, collected by one agency, SLA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under the previous framework, landowners and developers have to pay to either the URA or SLA, a Development Charge or a Temporary Development Levy or a Differential Premium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, now under the new Act, the LBC will replace all these previous charges and collected by just one agency, SLA.

sections.label: Progressive Budget moves welcomed
sections.summary: Speaker welcomes progressive Budget moves including higher salaries for lower-income workers, higher income and wealth taxes, and GST with vouchers and rebates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The more money you have, the better the life you lead, the more you can afford to pay for other people's children's education and other people’s healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I welcome the progressive moves in the Budget: the uplift in salaries for lower-income workers, the higher income taxes for the rich, the wealth taxes, and the combination of GST with GST Vouchers and other rebates.

sections.label: Electricity bill increase
sections.summary: Over the past few months, his electricity bill rose from $120 to $200 a month, an increase of $80.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Over the past few months, his electricity bill has gone up from $120 a month to $200 or by $80 a month.

sections.label: Inflation assumptions and Household Support Package
sections.summary: MP asks Finance Minister what inflation assumptions shaped the $560 million Household Support Package and whether more support can be given, including to middle-income earners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Some of these, we expect to come down in due time, as MTI has previously shared, but the developments in Ukraine and the continued disruption of supply chains, give rise to concerns that this situation might go on past the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Finance Minister, what assumptions of inflationary trends were made in developing the $560 million Household Support Package and whether more support can be given, including to the middle-income, for whom ComCare is not an option.

sections.label: Attracting Beyond Great companies
sections.summary: The Government, led by EDB, can proactively attract and nurture Beyond Great companies to anchor in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government, led by EDB, can proactively attract and nurture Beyond Great companies to anchor in Singapore.

sections.label: Reskilling workforce and reexamining education system
sections.summary: Moves made are not enough; reskilling and upskilling must accelerate and the education system must be reexamined from early childhood to work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We have made significant moves since then, but it is still not enough.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We must continue to accelerate the reskilling and upskilling of our workforce for a more digital, more green future and, over the long term, we must reexamine the entire education system from early childhood all the way to work, to enable learning at the right time, at the right place, on a personalised learning journey.

sections.label: Comprehensive social security system
sections.summary: A comprehensive social security system fit for Singapore's demographic profile has been built with Workfare, Silver Support and Progressive Wage Model.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As I have alluded to earlier in my speech, we have built, over time, a comprehensive social security system fit for our demographic profile with Workfare, Silver Support and Progressive Wage Model – really quite game changing.

sections.label: Permanent growth dividend proposal
sections.summary: Speaker suggests exploring a permanent growth dividend tied to GDP or Budget surpluses, with payouts based on wealth or income, partly cash and partly CPF.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The support package has elements of this but, if we want to be more inclusive, could we explore a more structural change to provide a permanent growth dividend tied to GDP or Budget surpluses, with different payouts, of course, based on wealth or income, partly in cash, partly in CPF, that give every Singaporean an additional stake in the nation's economic progress, reinforcing that we win and lose as a team.

sections.label: National culture, GST and cost of living
sections.summary: Speaker hopes for more nation-building and Malay community networks, notes the $6.6b Assurance package offsets GST for most, and urges swift support if high costs persist.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I hope more will be done to build a positive national culture and that through the formation of networks, mentorship and communities, the Malay community can be lifted by a positive spirit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I know many are unhappy about introducing GST in next year, but I also know that with the $6.6b Assurance package, the vast majority of our community will not be affected by the GST increase at all until 5 or even 10 years or more from now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Indeed, some will get a GST bonus in the interim.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Separate from GST, there are valid concerns about cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will move swiftly to support Singaporeans even more if the high costs persist.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model for low-wage workers
sections.summary: The Progressive Wage Model was developed to uplift salaries and skills of low-wage workers without dis-employment risks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For example, when we developed the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) to uplift the salaries and skills of our low-wage workers without exposing them to dis-employment risks.

sections.label: Company Training Committees set up
sections.summary: Since Koh Poh Koon started CTCs in April 2019, 826 CTCs have been set up with large organisations and SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Since Brother Koh Poh Koon started the CTCs in April 2019, we have set up 826 CTCs so far, with both large organisations and SMEs.

sections.label: Government funding for NTUC CTCs
sections.summary: The Government agreed to provide NTUC $100 million to scale up CTCs, including a $70 million grant for transformation plans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement would also like to thank the Government for agreeing to our proposal to provide NTUC with $100 million to scale up our CTCs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: And this includes a $70 million grant to help CTC companies implement their transformation plans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This will give NTUC additional resources to work with our CTC companies and co-fund their proposals to raise productivity, re-design jobs, upskill workers and improve work prospects by helping every worker to become a better worker through training, making every job a better job through job redesign and then matching the better workers to the better jobs through effective job placement.

sections.label: NTUC target of 2,500 CTCs
sections.summary: NTUC will go beyond 1,000 CTCs this year to at least 2,500 by 2025, using $30 million to expand ITOs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: NTUC will go beyond our original target of forming 1,000 CTCs by this year to achieve a more ambitious goal of having at least 2,500 CTCs by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will make good use of the $30 million funding from the Government to expand our team of Industry Training Officers (ITOs) and enlarge our network of CTCs to benefit more workers and more companies.

sections.label: Partnerships helping workers like Nur
sections.summary: NTUC and e2i partner social enterprises and agencies to help workers, and the Jobs Growth Incentive includes higher support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: NTUC and e2i have been partnering social enterprises and agencies like Agape Connecting People, Yellow Ribbon, Singapore Prison Service and SG Enable to help our fellow Singaporean workers like Nur and many others.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: I am also glad the Jobs Growth Incentive, which has been extended to September 2022, will continue to include higher support for employers who hire persons with disabilities and ex-offenders.

sections.label: NTUC supports foreigner inflow moves
sections.summary: NTUC supports Government moves to differentiate foreigner inflow and enforce action against errant employers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: NTUC supports the Government’s moves to differentiate the inflow of foreigners to offer better protection for Singaporean workers and to take firm enforcement action against errant employers to send a clear message.

sections.label: Differentiated approach for good employers
sections.summary: A differentiated approach recognises good employers who built a strong Singaporean Core, giving them advantages in Government projects, grants and work pass applications.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: A differentiated approach is also fairer to good employers who have invested resources in building a strong Singaporean Core and developed positive relations with the Labour Movement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: These companies add value to their workers and to the community and we should recognise their contributions in tangible ways, for example, by giving them a competitive advantage over their peers, including in areas, such as Government projects, grants and work pass applications.

sections.label: Employees in expanded job roles
sections.summary: 115 employees have taken on expanded job roles in Air Service Management, Passenger Services, Load Control and Cargo Services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: A 115 employees have taken on expanded job roles in Air Service Management, Passenger Services, Load Control and Cargo Services.

sections.label: Tripartite Academies for skills mismatch
sections.summary: Tripartite Academies bring unions, employers and Government agencies together to identify industry-specific skills requirements so workers receive job-relevant training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Some workers also feel frustrated when the new skills they acquire after going through training are not a good fit with what employers are looking for.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We propose to address the skills mismatch by forming Tripartite Academies, where we bring together unions, employers and Government agencies to jointly identify industry-specific skills requirements, so that workers can receive job-relevant training that prepare them for jobs that employers offer.

sections.label: Singapore Bus Academy partnership
sections.summary: The Singapore Bus Academy was formed in 2016 by Land Transport Authority, National Transport Workers' Union and public bus operators to train bus captains and technicians.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Singapore Bus Academy (SGBA) was formed in 2016 as a partnership between Land Transport Authority, National Transport Workers' Union and the public bus operators to train bus captains and technicians.

sections.label: Tourism Careers Hub training courses
sections.summary: Tourism Careers Hub will provide customised training courses on employer-required skillsets, including safety, security, customer service, digital skills and eco-tourism knowledge.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Tourism Careers Hub will provide customised training courses focusing on skillsets that employers require, including traditional areas such as safety, security and customer service as well as emerging areas such as digital skills and knowledge in eco-tourism.

sections.label: Tripartite Academies in other sectors
sections.summary: The Labour Movement is discussing with employers and Government agencies to explore Tripartite Academies in advanced manufacturing, retail, logistics, security, healthcare and maritime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Besides tourism, the Labour Movement is discussing with employers and Government agencies to explore setting up Tripartite Academies in sectors such as advanced manufacturing, retail, logistics, security, healthcare and maritime.

sections.label: Company Training Committee at Chang Cheng
sections.summary: Chang Cheng Group and the Food, Drinks and Allied Workers Union set up a Company Training Committee to train and upgrade close to 1,000 employees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Chang Cheng Group and the Food, Drinks and Allied Workers Union worked together to set up a Company Training Committee (CTC) to develop plans for employee training, business transformation and job redesign, to train and upgrade the skills of all their employees (close to 1,000) and give them better job prospects.

sections.label: Lowering Dependency Ratio Ceiling and NTUC grant
sections.summary: A worker representative welcomes the lowered Dependency Ratio Ceiling and the $100 million grant to NTUC for Company Training Committees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As someone who represent workers, I am very heartened with the announcement on the lowering of the Dependency Ratio Ceiling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the announcement of the $100 million grant to NTUC shows the Government's trust and confidence in NTUC's efforts to enhance the capabilities of workers alongside their employers through the Company Training Committees or CTC.

sections.label: Foreign Dependency Ratio and qualifying salary
sections.summary: The Foreign Dependency Ratio is cut from one to seven to one to five, and minimum qualifying salaries rise by $500, drawing unhappiness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recent announcement on the reduction of Foreign Dependency Ratio from one is to seven to one is to five, is a positive move to reduce reliance on foreign workers, but raising the minimum qualifying salary by $500 for Employment Pass and S Pass applicants created some misconception and unhappiness because, some see this as a move to increase wages of foreign workers but our Singaporeans do not get similar adjustments over the same period of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the rationale is to ensure employability of our local workforce, MOM needs to clearly show how the increase in the qualifying salary of S Pass and Employment Pass has benefited the local workforce and resulted in the overall increase in wages for Singaporeans.

sections.label: NTUC support for company training committees
sections.summary: NTUC welcomes the Government setting aside $100 million to scale up company training committees for companies' transformation plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: NTUC is very heartened by the Government's strong support in setting aside $100 million to scale up the company training committees (CTCs) to support companies' transformation plans.

sections.label: NTUC Learning Hub training places
sections.summary: Companies in hard-hit sectors reskilled employees, and NTUC Learning Hub recorded over 500,000 training places and upskilled more than 300,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This allowed companies from hard-hit sectors such as aviation, hospitality and among others, to reskill and upskill their employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that NTUC Learning Hub has achieved a record of over 500,000 training places and upskill more than 300,000 workers since the start of the pandemic.

sections.label: Singapore inflation in December 2021 and January 2022
sections.summary: Singapore's overall inflation jumped to 4% year-on-year in December 2021 and remained at 4% in January 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's overall inflation in December 2021 has jumped to 4% on a year-on-year basis and has remained at 4% in January 2022.

sections.label: GST vouchers and support criteria
sections.summary: Welcomes GST Voucher, doubled U-Save rebates and higher GST Cash Payment income criterion, and asks Government to review income criteria of support schemes to prevent the cliff effect for lower middle-income families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Aside from GST Voucher and doubling the U-Save rebates applicable to all HDB households for the remaining quarter in 2022, we also appreciate the increase of annual assessable income to $34,000 as a qualifying criterion for the GST Cash Payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us also not forget the group of lower middle-income workers, who are earning slightly more than lower-income individuals, but their families are also struggling with increasing daily expenses, yet they are losing access to Government support schemes as they have just fallen short slightly of the income criteria of these support schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can review the income criteria of various support schemes such as Kindergarten, Student Care and Childcare Subsidies, CPF Housing Grants, to prevent the "cliff effect" and better support the lower middle-income family.

sections.label: NTUC social enterprises
sections.summary: States there are 10 NTUC social enterprises under the NTUC Enterprise group, including FairPrice, FoodFare, Kopitiam, First Campus and Learning Hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, there are 10 NTUC social enterprises under the NTUC Enterprise group, ranging from FairPrice, FoodFare, Kopitiam, First Campus, Learning Hub and more.

sections.label: NTUC support for companies and workers
sections.summary: NTUC supports companies to form CTCs and provides business strategy planning, job redesign and workforce training, and hopes Government supports middle-income earners and reviews support scheme criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: NTUC is here to support companies to form CTCs and through the Training and Placement ecosystem, we will provide support for business strategy planning, job redesign and workforce training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Most importantly, building the pipeline of local talents for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I really hope Government hears our call for greater support for middle-income earners to cope with the increasing cost of living as well as constantly reviewing the criteria of various support schemes to ensure this group of workers does not fall through the cracks.

sections.label: NTUC-SNEF PME taskforce recommendations
sections.summary: The NTUC-SNEF PME taskforce consulted over 10,000 PMEs and stakeholders and presented nine recommendations under four thrusts to Minister Tan See Leng and MOM on 21 October 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Last year, the NTUC-SNEF PME taskforce, which I co-chaired, consulted more than 10,000 PMEs and stakeholders to understand their concerns, needs, aspirations and fears at the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: NTUC and SNEF have together deliberated the various challenges and concerns faced to arrive at nine recommendations under four key thrusts, which was presented to Minister Tan See Leng and MOM on 21 October 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to elaborate on four of the most urgent tasks on hand to enhance workplace fairness, employment and employability for our PMEs, which are: first, strengthening the Singaporean Core through enhancing the Employment Pass framework; second, imposing a penalty framework for egregious cases of workplace fairness; third, protecting the confidentiality of whistle-blowers of discriminatory practices; and lastly, four, helping mature PMEs to transit into new roles through short term salary support.

sections.label: Employment Pass application review points
sections.summary: Hopes MOM will include a point system in the EP application review process factoring in sectoral input, local worker hiring and development, and nationality diversity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I look forward to MOM sharing more details of the refined EP framework at the Committee of Supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I hope that MOM will take in our NTUC-SNEF PME Taskforce’s recommendation for the enhancement of the EP application review process and include a point system which factors in: (a) sectoral input; (b) whether the employer has been hiring and developing local workers; and (c) the diversity of nationalities within the companies.

sections.label: Penalising egregious companies
sections.summary: Says more must be done to penalise the small proportion of egregious companies exploiting the system so local PMEs receive fair opportunities while maintaining Singapore's economic competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: While there have been many measures and policies, even with the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) set up over the years, more needs to be done to penalise the small proportion of egregious companies that are out to exploit the system, so that local PMEs can continue to receive fair opportunities and treatment while maintaining Singapore’s economic competitiveness.

sections.label: Mature PMEs retrenchment vulnerability
sections.summary: The NTUC-SNEF PME Taskforce Report finds mature PMEs are particularly precarious and vulnerable when retrenched or unemployed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The findings of the NTUC-SNEF PME Taskforce Report shows that mature PMEs are in a particularly precarious and vulnerable situation when they are retrenched or unemployed.

sections.label: Job discrimination and Jobs Growth Incentive
sections.summary: Half faced discrimination in job search or workplaces, and the Jobs Growth Incentive will be extended to September 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Half of them expressed that they faced some form of discrimination during their job search or at their current workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Some also held the perception that companies are not open to hiring workers who are aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Thus, I am heartened that in this Budget, the Jobs Growth Incentive (JGI), which supports employers to expand local hiring from September 2020 to March 2022, will be extended to September 2022.

sections.label: PWCS wage co-funding support
sections.summary: The Government will co-fund wage increases of eligible resident employees from 2022 to 2026 under the PWCS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Under this scheme, the Government will co-fund wage increases of eligible resident employees from 2022 to 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The introduction of the PWCS is a step in the right direction and will go a long way in uplifting and supporting lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As more sectors and occupations are incorporated into the PWM, there will be a greater need to re-think the duration of transitory support new sectors will receive under the PWCS beyond 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to know how new sectors incorporated into the PWM between 2025 and 2026 will be supported.

sections.label: Call for PWM in two sectors
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to seriously consider implementing the PWM in the two sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to take this opportunity to call on the Government to seriously consider our proposal to implement PWM in the two sectors.

sections.label: Migrant worker insurance membership fee
sections.summary: Migrant workers would be insured up to $10,000 for a membership fee of about $24 per annum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In exchange for a membership fee of about $24 per annum, our migrant workers would be insured up to $10,000 in term life insurance against critical illnesses, non-work-related death as well as total and permanent disability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: To ensure that our migrant workers are insured within and beyond the workplace, I call on the Government to mandate or incentivise companies to sponsor the membership fee for their workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Early last year, it was reported that more than 97% of employers with foreign workers living in dormitories were paying salaries electronically, up from 76% before the requirement was introduced in April 2020.

sections.label: NTUC MENDAKI Malay workers collaboration
sections.summary: NTUC formalised a Memorandum of Understanding with Yayasan MENDAKI to advance Employment and Employability for Malay workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: On 24 February, through a Memorandum of Understanding, NTUC formalised our collaboration with Yayasan MENDAKI with both organisations tapping on our respective networks and resources to advance Employment and Employability for Malay workers in Singapore.

sections.label: Company Training Committees with NTUC
sections.summary: NTUC will partner companies to set up Company Training Committees bringing unions and employers together for firm-level transformation and worker training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In line with a Malay proverb that tells one to make an effort to achieve one’s desired outcome - NTUC will also partner companies to set up Company Training Committees, or CTCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As highlighted by Brother Chee Hong Tat and other parliamentary colleagues earlier, this CTC model brings together the unions and employers to develop concrete firm-level transformation plans, including the relevant training needed by their workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Through the CTC companies, we can multiply our impact to help more workers train and upskill.

sections.label: Government and NTUC worker commitment
sections.summary: The Government and NTUC commit to helping workers at every step and fighting for a fairer, more progressive society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As we chart a new forward together, the Government and NTUC are committed to helping workers in every step of the way and will continue our fight for a fairer and more progressive society for all.

sections.label: Low pay in food and retail
sections.summary: About 60% of food services and 45% of retail full-time resident workers earn at or below the 20th wage percentile.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Despite this, even till today, some 60% of food services and 45% of retail full-time resident workers are earning at or less than the 20th wage percentile of the local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In many international standards among OECD countries, percentile 20 defines the threshold for low pay.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model concept
sections.summary: The Progressive Wage Model links wage increases with productivity increases through upskilling, technology investments and career pathways.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therein, the concept of PWM is critical as it marries wage increases with productivity increases through upskilling, investments in technology and career pathways.

sections.label: Study on gig worker poverty
sections.summary: An Institute of Public Policy study warns food delivery and private hire vehicle workers risk being trapped in poverty and precarity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Indeed, in the recent study by the Institute of Public Policy just released yesterday, researchers warn of food delivery and private hire vehicle workers facing risks of becoming trapped in poverty and precarity.

sections.label: Protection for gig workers
sections.summary: Platforms like Grab and Deliveroo offer riders accident insurance, and NTUC Learning Hub introduces career conversion classes for drivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As we seek to maintain the flexibility and ease of entry into the gig economy that current circumstances allow for, it is imperative that the companies and platforms share our workers' sentiments and work towards providing better protection for our freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I am heartened to see some platforms putting in place their own measures to protect their riders, with delivery platforms such as Grab and Deliveroo offering their riders basic accident insurance coverage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement, through NTUC Learning Hub, has also started to introduce career conversion classes to protect the long-term livelihoods of our drivers who intend to move out of the industry.

sections.label: Standardised insurance for workers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a standardised level of insurance should apply to all workers in the same plight instead of basic insurance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Instead of basic insurance, should we not look towards a standardised level of insurance applied to all workers in the same plight?

sections.label: Mothercare new hires mothers
sections.summary: The passage states that mothers with young children were 40% of Mothercare's new hires in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: When I visited Mothercare recently, I was delighted to note that mothers with young children were 40% of their new hires in 2021.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model start dates
sections.summary: The passage states the Progressive Wage Model will commence in the 3rd quarter of 2022 for retail and 1st quarter of 2023 for F&B.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, Sir, the Progressive Wage Model will commence in the 3rd quarter of 2022 for the retail industry and 1st quarter of 2023 for the F&B industry.

sections.label: Low-income workers and wage credit
sections.summary: The passage states 60% of food services and 45% of retail workers are low-income, and a five-year Progressive Wage Credit Scheme was announced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Some 60% of food services and 45% of retail sector workers are classified as low-income workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In this Budget, the Government announced a five-year Progressive Wage Credit Scheme to help stablise the wage of the F&B and retail sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, improving the situation of low-wage Singaporeans requires the cooperation of other stakeholders.

sections.label: Young NTUC youth employment study
sections.summary: The passage states a Young NTUC study of 1,500 young Singaporeans found two in three anxious about employment and one in two certain of their career path.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Recently, Young NTUC commissioned a study involving 1,500 young Singaporeans from age 16 to 35.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Perhaps, unsurprisingly, two out of three youths are anxious about the employment landscape, finding it challenging to navigate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Only one in two youths is certain of their career path and believe that they are provided with adequate career opportunities.

sections.label: Lowering SkillsFuture minimum age
sections.summary: The passage states shorter economic cycles require considering lowering the minimum age for SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The much shorter economic cycles require us to consider lowering the minimum age for SkillsFuture.

sections.label: SG Youth Action Plan vision
sections.summary: The SG Youth Action Plan shows youth's vision for Singapore in 2025: social inclusivity, sustainability, mental well-being and a stronger social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the SG Youth Action Plan has shown us our youth’s vision for Singapore in 2025 – social inclusivity, sustainability, mental well-being, and the need to strengthen our social compact.

sections.label: Budget 2022 theme
sections.summary: There is an urgent need for deeper conversations, leading to the theme of Budget 2022: Charting the Way Forward Together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We have an urgent need for deeper conversations to chart the way forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This brings us to the theme of Budget 2022 – Charting the Way Forward Together.

sections.label: NTUC mental well-being and youth
sections.summary: NTUC launched a WSQ on peer-to-peer support and will champion the aspirations and needs of younger Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: NTUC has launched a WSQ on peer-to-peer support and endeavours to work with all stakeholders to advance mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In NTUC, we will champion the aspirations and needs of our younger Singaporeans.

sections.label: Rising prices and freight costs
sections.summary: Prices rose 20%, sugar and salt 30%, and shipping raw sugar from Thailand rose from under $200 to $1,000 per container.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Prices have gone up by 20%, sugar and salt are up 30%, and the freight cost of shipping raw sugar from Thailand to Singapore has increased from what used to be less than $200 per 20-foot full container load, is now $1,000.

sections.label: Businesses reporting higher costs
sections.summary: 57% of Singapore businesses surveyed saw costs rise this year, nearly double the 28.8% last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For sure, some 57% of Singapore businesses surveyed saw their costs rise this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: That is nearly double the 28.8% who did so last year.

sections.label: Stretch Your Dollar programme
sections.summary: Two Mondays ago, the "Stretch Your Dollar" programme was announced, giving a 5% discount on 100 essential items every Friday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Just two Mondays ago, we announced the "Stretch Your Dollar" programme to give a 5% discount on 100 essential items every Friday.

sections.label: Over $441 million given out
sections.summary: The passage states that over $441 million have been given out when these are grouped together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In fact, when I group all these together, over $441 million have been given out.

sections.label: Affordability, income support, scheme awareness
sections.summary: It asks for whole-of-Government and whole-of-society coordination to keep basic items affordable, support those with lost or reduced incomes, and help more people know about and apply for schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: First, can we on a whole-of-Government and whole-of-society basis, coordinate, encourage efforts which keep basic items affordable, to help cope with the cost of living?

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Second, keep looking out for those whose incomes have been lost or reduced during the pandemic and to provide support for those who might fall through the cracks, such as those with limited family support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And related to the second, perhaps it is not just a matter of having more schemes, but helping more people become aware of and applying for such schemes.

sections.label: Price Kaki app expansion
sections.summary: The app has been downloaded over 80,000 times, and CASE will expand it this year with more retailers, products, services, cooked food stalls and grocery items.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Since its launch, the app has been downloaded more than 80,000 times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: CASE will expand Price Kaki this year, with more retailers, more products and more services, so as to benefit more consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We will increase the coverage of cooked food stalls from the current 114 hawker centres to cover an additional 200 foodcourts and coffee shops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: CASE will also increase the coverage of groceries and household essentials on the app from 4,000 to 10,000 items.

sections.label: Mandatory unit pricing call
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to introduce mandatory unit pricing for supermarkets and grocery retailers in Singapore to tackle shrinkflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: To tackle this shrinkflation, I would like to call on the Government to introduce mandatory unit pricing for supermarkets and grocery retailers in Singapore.

sections.label: $100 million for NTUC training committees
sections.summary: NTUC career coaches found mid-career PMETs often neglect skills upgrading, and the Government is committing $100 million to scale NTUC's company training committees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Our NTUC's career coaches have found that many mid-career PMETs often neglect to go for skills upgrading because they were too caught up with day-to-day work schedules and very wide-ranging family responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
