sentences.text: That is why I am glad that the Government is committing $100 million to scale NTUC's company training committees (CTCs).

sections.label: Workplace mental health initiatives
sections.summary: The speaker has spoken on workplace mental health, and the Government worked with the Labour Movement on initiatives including the November 2020 Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-being at Workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Over the years, I have been speaking both inside and outside of this House on the importance of maintaining good workplace mental health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government has worked closely with the Labour Movement on various initiatives, notably the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-being at Workplaces back in November 2020, which provides guidance on after-hours work communications.

sections.label: NTUC survey on work stress
sections.summary: An NTUC survey of 1,000 young working adults found over 40% reported poor work-life balance and 42% felt insufficient mental well-being support at work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to a recent NTUC survey of 1,000 young working adults, over 40% reported poor work-life balance and work stress due to longer working hours and heavier workload since the start of the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Forty-two percent of the respondents felt that there was insufficient mental well-being support at their workplaces.

sections.label: CPF contribution rates for older workers
sections.summary: The first step to improve CPF contribution rates for workers aged 55 to 70 was carried out in January, with the next tranche in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In January this year, the first step to improve the CPF contribution rates for older workers aged 55 to 70 was carried out.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This is part of the journey to harmonise CPF contribution rates for workers up to age 60 by the year 2030, as part of overall measures to help strengthen the retirement adequacy of Singaporean workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I, therefore, welcome our Finance Minister’s announcement in this year’s Budget that the next tranche of CPF contribution rate improvements would be carried out in 2023.

sections.label: Mature workers' employment rates rise
sections.summary: Mature workers' employment rates rose from 27.6% in 2019 to 28.5% in 2020 to 31.7% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The combined result of tripartite and Government resolve and action has been a steady rise in mature workers' employment rates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: It improved from 27.6% in 2019 to 28.5% in 2020 to 31.7% in 2021.

sections.label: Study on affordable senior day care
sections.summary: The speaker believes more must be done and calls for a thorough study on enabling affordable senior day care services at scale.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: But I believe that this is not sufficient and we have to do more.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I believe that it is timely for a very thorough study to be carried out on how to enable appropriate affordable senior day care services, whether they be homecare or day-focused institutions, to be made available, at scale, that would also be sustainable for the service providers to provide.

sections.label: Scaling up senior day care services
sections.summary: The speaker says the expansion of senior day care services must be studied and implemented with appropriate conditions to forestall workforce departures and higher demand for foreign domestic help.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Of course, the details are different and the conditionality for providing such affordable and accessible senior day care at scale is not identical but will have to be studied.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: But we must study this expansion of such day care services in earnest and, through policy direction, implement a scaling up of such services with appropriate conditions so that we can forestall a surge in local workforce departures in the medium term, or a huge further increase in demand for foreign domestic help to look after the seniors.

sections.label: Tripartite focus on reskilling older workers
sections.summary: The speaker calls for a tripartite focus to identify priority sectors and occupations for reskilling older workers, thanking the Government for $100 million supporting NTUC's efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: To forestall this, I call for a specific tripartite focus to identify such priority sectors and occupations for re-skilling so that older workers holding these current jobs roles can be reskilled and be part of their firm's future even as their companies transform.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In this regard, I join my colleagues in thanking the Government of the investment of $100 million to work together and support NTUC's efforts in this area.

sections.label: Play, KidSTART and UPLIFT expansion
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes more investment to scale up KidSTART nationwide and expand the UPLIFT Community Network for children in disadvantaged families.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Opportunities for deliberate play and exploration will allow children to pick up social interaction and problem-solving skills beyond what books can offer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I welcome the announcement that we will be investing more in our children to scale up the KidSTART programme nationwide and expand into a nationwide UPLIFT Community Network to support more children in disadvantaged families.

sections.label: KidSTART and UPLIFT tackle inequality
sections.summary: The speaker says enhanced KidSTART and upscaled UPLIFT show commitment to tackle inequality early and give every child a chance in Primary school.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, the move for an enhanced KidSTART and upscaled UPLIFT programme underlines our strong commitment to tackle inequality at the earliest juncture possible and ensures that every child is given the opportunity to discover the joy of exploration and play and importantly, stand a fighting chance when they enter Primary school.

sections.label: Whole-of-society approach to education
sections.summary: The speaker urges a whole-of-society approach to change mindsets on education and shift from Assessment of Learning to Journey of Learning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I urge this call in unison for a "whole-of-society approach" to change the mindsets on education, from daily school issues to major examinations and how we perceive success and learning as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is about time to change this "Assessment of Learning" culture to a "Journey of Learning".

sections.label: Reviewing longer duration for students
sections.summary: The speaker suggests it may be time to review whether a slightly longer duration would let students develop better and pursue interests.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Perhaps, it is time to review if a slightly longer duration would allow students to develop better, to get that much needed time and space to equip themselves and pursue these interests.

sections.label: Mental health of younger adults
sections.summary: Citing MOH's survey finding poor mental health highest among adults aged 18 to 29, the speaker calls for expanded outreach and more psychiatric services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In November last year, MOH published its National Population Health Survey and found that younger adults aged between 18 and 29 had the highest proportion of poor mental health, for about 21.5%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I call on the task force to expand outreach and support for this particular group and hope that with the rising numbers as a whole, we can also increase the number of psychiatrics services that we made available.

sections.label: Welcoming KidSTART and UPLIFT scale-up
sections.summary: On education, the speaker welcomes the announcement to scale up the KidSTART and UPLIFT programmes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As for education, I welcome the announcement to scale up the KidSTART and UPLIFT programmes.

sections.label: Inter-Agency Task Force on mental health
sections.summary: An Inter-Agency Task Force was established, showing the Government is concerned and acted against mental health stigmatisation and to support Singaporeans' needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The establishment of an Inter-Agency Task Force shows that the Government is concerned and took action against mental health stigmatisation and supporting the needs of Singaporeans.

sections.label: GST hikes and inflation
sections.summary: The GST hikes will further exacerbate inflationary pressure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The GST hikes will further exacerbate inflationary pressure.

sections.label: Healthcare spending and GST
sections.summary: The Finance Minister said healthcare spending could rise from $11 billion in 2019 to $27 billion in 2030, prompting questions on GST increases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister has shared that healthcare spending could increase from $11 billion in 2019 to $27 billion in 2030 based on current trend.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, does this mean that we would have to raise GST by 11% just to fund the additional healthcare spending?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Are we looking at 18% to 20% GST by 2030?

sections.label: Land sale proceeds as revenue
sections.summary: The Workers' Party suggested up to 20% of land sale proceeds as revenue, while PSP proposes taking them as revenue over the lease period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In Budget 2018, Workers' Party suggested that up to 20% of land sale proceeds be used as revenue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Then Finance Minister Heng said, with reference to land sold on 99-year lease, that, I quote, "If you are rigorous about it, you really ought to be spending no more than 1% of that land sale proceeds".

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This statement, while true, paints an incomplete picture and is, therefore, misleading.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It does not address what happens over time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: PSP proposes that land sale proceeds be taken as revenue over the period of the lease.

sections.label: F1 race subsidy
sections.summary: From FY2022 to FY2028, the Government is subsidising the F1 race at over $80 million per year, over $560 million in total.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: From FY2022 to FY2028, the Government is subsidising the F1 race to the tune of over $80 million per year and that works out to be over $560 million.

sections.label: SPH Media Trust payment
sections.summary: A $900 million payment to SPH Media Trust over five years is described as another dubious expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Another dubious expenditure is the $900 million payment to SPH Media Trust over five years.

sections.label: HDB land payments to SLA
sections.summary: HDB pays SLA about $3 billion to $4 billion each year to purchase land.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Each year, HDB pays about $3 billion to $4 billion to SLA for purchase of land.

sections.label: MTI TRECS electricity scheme
sections.summary: MTI's Temporary Electricity Contracting Support Scheme, or TRECS, offered monthly fixed price plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Hope came in the form of MTI’s very popular Temporary Electricity Contracting Support Scheme, or TRECS, which offered monthly fixed price plans.

sections.label: Energy rebate proposal question
sections.summary: A question asks whether MOF and the Government would consider an energy rebate like U-Save Vouchers if expanding TRECS is not viable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Would MOF be willing, would the Government be willing to consider providing an energy rebate equivalent to, for example, the U-Save Vouchers given to residents, if expanding the TRECS programme is not viable?

sections.label: Study of S Pass policy
sections.summary: A question asks whether Government would direct a think tank to study the S Pass and E Pass policy's effectiveness and local talent pool.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In this regard, would Government direct a think tank to study the impact of this particular policy and decide: one, if this S Pass and E Pass policy is still effective to deter foreign hires and promote local hires; and two, if ways can be found to increase the pool of local talents in higher demand?

sections.label: Registered charities in Singapore
sections.summary: The passage states this strategy has long been adopted and there are more than 2,300 registered charities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This has been the adoption of this strategy for a long time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There are more than 2,300 registered charities in Singapore.

sections.label: Disability support and charity deficits
sections.summary: The passage lists disability issues including the cliff effect, housing needs, elderly parents' fears, and high-deficit programmes like residential homes and day care centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In the world of disability, for example, these include issues such as the "cliff effect" for many special-needs graduates who literally stop learning after the age of 18; the need for a continuum of residential housing options for especially disabled adults; the pleas for support by elderly parents too afraid to die for fear of what might happened to the ones they leave behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Some of these programmes such as residential homes and day care centres for the disabled are known to be high-ticket items that cause high operating deficits on charities, in the millions, and often insufficiently covered by Government grants, and these are spaces that only the lion-hearted or the clueless will enter.

sections.label: Tote Board Enhanced Fundraising flexibility
sections.summary: The Budget extends the Tote Board Enhanced Fundraising programme, and the speaker suggests flexibility so charities can hold one large campaign.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One case in point is Government’s partnership in this Budget to extend the Tote Board’s Enhanced Fundraising programme, or EFR, to incentivise fundraising.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: They have to organise five campaigns in a year if they wish to obtain maximum matching.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I feel there ought to be flexibility in the current EFR scheme, so that charities can focus to organise just one large successful fundraising campaign, be done with fundraising for the year, and focus their resources and their energy on the core business of serving their beneficiaries.

sections.label: Singapore stress and suicides
sections.summary: A TODAY survey found 68% of Singapore respondents called 2021 most stressful, and 2020 saw 452 suicides, up 13% from 400.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A survey reported by TODAY in October 2021 indicated that 68% of respondents in Singapore said they found 2021 to be the most stressful year they have experienced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2020, Singapore reported 452 suicides, a 13% increase compared to 400 cases the year before.

sections.label: AIA mental illness insurance take-up
sections.summary: AIA, which launched Singapore's first mental illness insurance policy in January 2019, said Beyond Critical Care take-up rose over 470% from 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: AIA, which launched the first insurance policy in Singapore to cover mental illness in January 2019, said the take-up rate for its Beyond Critical Care plan rose by more than 470% compared with the same period in 2020.

sections.label: Youth financial prospects survey
sections.summary: A TODAY Youth Survey found 55% of 18- to 35-year-olds felt their financial prospects were dented by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A TODAY Youth Survey found 55 % of 18- to 35-year-olds felt a dent in their financial prospects as a result of COVID-19.

sections.label: Traineeship and Jobs Support funding
sections.summary: In 2020 the Government set aside $100 million for a traineeship scheme, and Budget 2022 sets aside $500 million for a Jobs and Business Support Package.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2020, for example, the Government set aside $100 million to fund a traineeship scheme as a stop-gap measure to help new graduates increase employability amid a weak job market due to the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In Budget 2022, a total of $500 million for a Jobs and Business Support Package will be set aside to support workers and businesses in segments of the economy that are facing slower recoveries.

sections.label: Singapore core inflation increase
sections.summary: MAS and MTI recently reported a 2.4% increase in Singapore's core inflation compared to a year ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   MAS and MTI recently reported a 2.4% increase in Singapore's core inflation compared to a year ago.

sections.label: NTU study on STEM women
sections.summary: An NTU study last year found 58% of women with STEM qualifications entered STEM careers, versus 70% of men.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A study by NTU last year showed that only 58% of women with STEM qualifications had embarked in careers in STEM-related fields, compared to 70% of men with the same qualifications.

sections.label: Support for Budget 2022
sections.summary: The speaker supports Budget 2022's steps, from healthcare spending to climate change action, and believes common ground can be found.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: From increased healthcare spending to care for our seniors, to heeding the call to tackle climate change despite the increased complexities that threaten to pull us in different directions, I support the steps taken in Budget 2022 and believe we can and will find common ground to work together, despite our differences, towards progress for all.

sections.label: Workfare recipients affected by criterion
sections.summary: About 20,000 Workfare recipients, all casual or part-time workers, are estimated to be affected by the criterion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: First, we estimate that around 20,000 Workfare recipients will be affected by the criterion, all of whom are casual or part-time workers.

sections.label: LQS part-time local pay
sections.summary: Under the new LQS requirement, firms hiring foreign workers must pay all part-time locals at least $9 per hour.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: With the new LQS requirement, firms that hire foreign workers must pay all of their locals working part-time at least $9 per hour.

sections.label: Concessionary Workfare for excluded groups
sections.summary: Persons with disabilities and ComCare recipients will receive concessionary Workfare payouts so they are not excluded from Workfare.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This includes persons with disabilities and ComCare recipients.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will provide them concessionary Workfare payouts so that they will not be excluded from Workfare.

sections.label: Multi-year foreign workforce road map
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance laid out a multi-year road map covering Employment Pass and S Pass salaries, levies, Dependency Ratio Ceiling and MYE.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance has laid out a multi-year road map to increase the qualifying salary for Employment Passes; increase the qualifying salary and levies for S Passes; reduce the Dependency Ratio Ceiling; dismantle the Man-Year Entitlement (MYE) system and adjust levies for the Construction and Process sectors.

sections.label: S Pass qualifying salary increase
sections.summary: The qualifying salary for new S Pass applications rises to $3,000, with existing holders unaffected until September 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We have given businesses six months' notice for the first move to take effect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This first move will increase the qualifying salary to $3,000 for new S Pass applications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In other words, come September this year, 2022, all existing S Pass holders are still not affected – the existing ones that are here, they are still not affected.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will only apply the new qualifying salary 18 months later, from September 2023.

sections.label: Tier 1 levy increase
sections.summary: The Tier 1 levy will be raised gradually to $650 by September 2025 in three steps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Tier 1 levy will be gradually raised to $650 by September 2025, in not just one step but three steps.

sections.label: Women not in labour force
sections.summary: About 20% or 260,000 women aged 25 to 64 are not in the labour force.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For a whole myriad of reasons, there are about 20% or 260,000 women aged 25 to 64 who are not in the labour force.

sections.label: Work Permit holders awaiting entry
sections.summary: As of end January 2022, around 46,000 approved Work Permit holders have yet to enter Singapore due to border controls.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As of end January 2022, there are around 46,000 approved Work Permit holders who have yet to enter Singapore due to border controls.

sections.label: GST increase revenue shortfall
sections.summary: The Workers' Party suggests doing away with the GST increase by raising other taxes, a $3.5 billion revenue shortfall.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party suggests that we can do away with the GST increase if we raise more taxes through other means.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: That is a revenue shortfall of $3.5 billion.

sections.label: Fair versus punitive GST load
sections.summary: There is a difference between a fair load and a punitive load, and the entire $3.5 billion GST amount cannot be loaded on those at the very top.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: But there is a significant difference between what constitutes a fair load and what constitutes a punitive load.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It is not possible to get the entire GST amount – the $3.5 billion – by loading it entirely on all those just at the very top.

sections.label: Taxes on top earners
sections.summary: It is not possible to have extremely punitive taxes on just the top 1% or 5%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Because it is not possible to have extremely punitive taxes on just the top 1% or the 5%.

sections.label: GST help and middle-class burden
sections.summary: Those with less get back more than they pay in additional GST, and the Workers' Party's approach would shift the tax burden onto the middle-class.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In fact, those with less would get back much more than what they pay in additional GST and we give generous help to those who need the help while everyone pays something.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It is both an individual and our collective responsibility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: And if we do what has been proposed and suggested, the middle-income, the upper-middle-income, those who have worked hard, who have done, perhaps, better than their parents' expectations and aspirations, they will feel betrayed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: If we take the Workers' Party's approach, we will, as a consequence, have to increasingly shift and raise the tax burden onto the middle-class.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: That, I believe, is the surest way to unravel and destroy our social compact and trust in our society and Singapore will not hold together.

sections.label: Help schemes for low earners
sections.summary: A person earning less than $500 would not qualify, but many help schemes are available.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In terms of the individual who works and gets less than $500, the current construct is that yes, in the absence of any other things, he or she would not qualify.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But there is an entire plethora of help schemes available.

sections.label: Punitive burden on top earners
sections.summary: The proposal could result in a very high disproportionate burden on the top 1% to 5%, which is not sustainable and is punitive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As far as the point about the taxes, the whole crux of this was for your team to consider that what you are proposing, consequentially, could result in very, very high disproportionate burden on the top 1% to 5%, that it is not sustainable and it is punitive.

sections.label: WIS should not be denied
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to reconsider so that WIS is not denied, since a smaller number means even less fiscal impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And it is in that spirit that I would forward and advance that they should not be denied the WIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I hope the Minister can reconsider this because if the number is already smaller, less than half the number that I quoted, I think it is figure 28 of the Labour Force statistics, then all the more, the impact, the fiscal impact is even less.

sections.label: Fixed $500 amount
sections.summary: The $500 is fixed at this particular point in time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The $500 is fixed at this particular point in time.

sections.label: Number about 20,000
sections.summary: Minister Tan shared that the number is about 20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: As Minister Tan shared, the number is about 20,000.

sections.label: Wealth tax lever and hole
sections.summary: Only the wealth tax lever approaches high-income individuals, with modest recovery of about $1.2 billion, while the $3.5 billion hole would be met by broader taxes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I say this because, if you look at the four levers that we have described, only one of these – what we had called "the wealth tax" lever – actually approaches the high-income, high net worth individuals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And even within that particular scenario, we had made very modest recovery assumptions, amounting to something in the order of $1.2 billion on wealth taxes alone.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Of course, the hole is $3.5 billion and so, it is important to understand that the rest of that hole would have been met by much more broad base forms of taxation.

sections.label: Workfare for part-time low-wage workers
sections.summary: Every low-wage part-time worker receiving ComCare will get Workfare, regardless of a bar, if earning less than $500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, can this group of people be extended some flexibility so that they can also get Workfare?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: So, I responded earlier and as I responded to Leader of Opposition, every low-wage worker who is working part-time, who is also receiving ComCare, will get Workfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Whether there is a bar or not, as long as you are low-income, part-time, working and getting a sum less than $500, you will get Workfare.

sections.label: ComCare and Workfare for low-income
sections.summary: As part of the concession, low-income workers getting ComCare get Workfare, differentiating them from casual workers not from low-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As what I have shared that as part of the concession given, for as long as you are low-income, you get ComCare, you will get Workfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: So, that differentiates our low-income workers from the casual workers who may not necessarily come from low-income households.

sections.label: January core inflation 2.4%
sections.summary: MAS and MTI official statistics indicate Singapore's core inflation in January rose to 2.4% year-on-year, the highest in over nine years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Official statistics taken from MAS and MTI indicate that Singapore's core inflation in January rose to 2.4% on a year-on-year basis, the highest level in more than nine years.

sections.label: ComCare Fund and GSTV top-ups
sections.summary: The Budget promises a $5 million ComCare Fund top-up over five years and $12 million over four years to self-help groups, with GSTV remaining and its income threshold increased.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Budget promises a top-up of the ComCare Fund by $5 million over five years, with another $12 million awarded over four years to self-help groups to better support low-income families.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am also heartened that the GST Voucher (GSTV) will remain to help defray some of the cost of living and that the assessable income threshold for GSTV will be increased to enable more Singaporeans to qualify for the rebates.

sections.label: Migrant workers rising costs
sections.summary: The migrant worker population is set to be more vulnerable than ever to rising costs and GST increases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I wish to highlight that the migrant worker population is set to be more vulnerable than ever to the effects of the rising costs and GST increases.

sections.label: Carbon tax and electricity bills
sections.summary: Carbon tax aims to reach $80 per tonne in 2030, possibly raising electricity bills, with U-save rebates cushioning the transition, and asks about more support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In terms of carbon taxes, aiming to increase it to $80 per tonne in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This may inevitably lead to the rise of electricity bills and coupled with the effect of inflation, many families and businesses are concerned about how they can cope.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is comforting that additional U-save rebates will be provided to cushion this transition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, as seen by how electricity prices may be affected by many factors, recently by geopolitical changes, could I ask if the Government is considering more support for households and businesses if the electricity bills increase more than expected?

sections.label: Permanent mental well-being office
sections.summary: It asks whether to go further than a transient inter-agency task force and form a permanent mental well-being office under PMO.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can we therefore go one step further from a transient inter-agency task force, to the formation of a permanent mental well-being office under PMO, such as one inspired by SNDGO?

sections.label: Tax on highest-end properties
sections.summary: The Budget sharply increases tax on the highest-end properties, raising only a few hundred million more each year, not the billions needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In this Budget, the Government is sharply increasing tax on the highest-end properties, but this will only raise a few hundred million more each year, not the billions that we need.

sections.label: Increasing NIRC rate to 60%
sections.summary: The NIRC rate is 50% today, and increasing it to 60% could raise enough to fully fund future healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, the NIRC rate is 50% and if we increase NIRC to say 60%, we can raise enough to fully fund future healthcare.

sections.label: NIRC formula and GST increase
sections.summary: The current 50-50 NIRC formula is just right, and increasing GST is the fairest way to raise needed revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is the most precious thing and Singaporeans should carry this on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, I think the current 50-50 formula for our NIRC is just right and we should resist the urge to spend more of NIR today, leaving less for tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: On the other hand, for GST, because and only because of the specific way in which GST has been designed here in Singapore, I believe that increasing GST is the fairest way for us to raise the revenues that we need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is the fairest way because a large proportion of GST – more than half of GST – is paid not by the average Singaporean but by foreigners working and living here, by tourists visiting Singapore and by a minority of Singaporeans who spend more.

sections.label: Assurance Package for lower-income family
sections.summary: A lower-income family of four in a 3-room flat will receive $5,010 under the Assurance Package from 2022 to 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Based on MOF's example, for a typical lower-income family – a couple with two young children in a 3-room flat, the husband the sole breadwinner – they will receive $5,010 under the Assurance Package from 2022 to 2026.

sections.label: Total support for typical family
sections.summary: With S&CC rebates, the family receives almost $7,400 in additional support over five years, totalling $9,200.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And on top of that, around $590 in Service and Conservancy Charges (S&CC) rebates, which have also been made a permanent feature of GST Vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, transitional support and permanent enhancements combined, this typical family will receive additional support totaling almost $7,400 over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The total additional support they will receive for the next five years comes up to $9,200 – very, very significant and I think a very strong signal of how we are strengthening our support for those with less.

sections.label: Workfare support increases
sections.summary: A 50-year-old gets $3,600 yearly, a 30-year-old $2,100, and persons with disabilities under 44 get $4,200 yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Specifically, a 50-year-old getting $2,500 per year in Workfare support today will get $3,600 per year in future; a 30-year-old young worker who has not been eligible for Workfare today will get $2,100 per year in future; and all persons with disabilities under the age of 44 who have been getting $1,700 per year today at the lowest tier of Workfare support will, in future, get the highest tier of support at $4,200 per year.

sections.label: GST as price-rise pretext
sections.summary: Cost of living is a real concern and a small minority of businesses may use GST as a pretext to raise prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Cost of living is a very real concern and, yes, a small minority of businesses may be using GST as a pretext to raise prices, perhaps, even ahead of the hike itself.

sections.label: GST and rising prices measures
sections.summary: The Budget addresses GST and rising prices with separate appropriate measures, and GST should not be a scapegoat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But let us start with all of us seeing the cost of living issue objectively and quite apart from GST factors because, ultimately, we have to refrain from making GST a strawman or a convenient scapegoat stopping us from doing what we ought to do as a people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: We can address both GST and rising prices with separate appropriate measures and this is what this Budget has done exactly.

sections.label: Raising GST considered necessary
sections.summary: All options were fully considered and raising GST is necessary, with the Budget as a first step.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: If the alternatives are really so straightforward, this Government must be mad to want to press on with GST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I think Singaporeans understand, deep down, that all options have been fully considered and raising GST is necessary – alongside other levers, of course, but raising GST is necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, let us focus our discourse ahead, our next steps, on how we can make this work, on what else we can do, on how we can all play a part, using this Budget as a “first step”.

sections.label: NIR cap and reserves
sections.summary: Mr Xie is asked whether raising the NIR contribution cap from 50% to 60% would still leave 40% going into compounded reserves for the next generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Xie said that we seek to leave behind something for the next generation and he spoke about the NIR ceiling, and he made a few very interesting points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I just wanted to ask him if he would acknowledge that if we have a 50% cap on the NIR contribution, that is, a cap of 50% that can be taken into the Budget every year, would the hon Member acknowledge that if we increase that cap from 50% to 60%, for example, there is still 40% that goes into the reserves and that gets compounded so that, therefore, you are not actually decreasing the reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: You are just increasing the reserves at a slower rate and you still will leave behind something more to the next generation, because that amount gets compounded and compounded as the years go by.

sections.label: NIRC rate judgement
sections.summary: The speaker says the current 50/50 NIRC rate is the right balance and other revenue levers should be looked at first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: And, so, to Mr Perera's question, I think it is really a question of judgement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: And if we look at the entire revenue mix, our NIRC rate now as it currently stands of 50/50 is, in my view, the right balance and we should look at other revenue levers in the first instance.

sections.label: Youth offender statistics
sections.summary: Youth offenders fell 43% over the past decade, from 4,174 in 2010 to 2,367 in 2020, but outrage of modesty and rape cases rose from 109 in 2016 to 162 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The overall number of youth offenders has fallen by 43% in the past decade.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In numerical terms, that translates to 4,174 in 2010, to 2,367 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The overarching statistics look dandy but there has been a worrying upward trend in the number of youth offenders who committed outrage of modesty and rape offences between 2016 and 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: More specifically, from 109 cases in 2016 to 162 in 2020.

sections.label: Job search talent trends
sections.summary: A 2021 Michael Page talent trends report indicated that 56% of Singapore workers see themselves searching for new jobs post-pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2021 talent trends report by Michael Page indicated that 56% of Singapore workers see themselves searching for new jobs post-pandemic.

sections.label: Work-life harmony grant suggestion
sections.summary: The speaker suggests Enterprise Singapore's Enterprise Development Grant include work life harmony as a fundable area, while raising reservations on high performance and lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to suggest that Enterprise Singapore’s Enterprise Development Grant include work life harmony as a specific fundable area, so that SMEs can avail of the grant to help them formulate work-life harmony programmes for their employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my support of these initiatives, I have some reservations on how we are approaching work-life harmony and this has to do with, first, how we can continue to encourage high performance and, second, how it applies to lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I read a recent survey by recruitment agency Randstad Singapore that showed that an equal number of respondents ranked “work-life balance” and “attractive salary and benefits” as the most important employee value proposition they looked for in an employer.

sections.label: Twitter paternal leave
sections.summary: Twitter offers its employees up to 20 weeks of paternal leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Twitter offers its employees up to 20 weeks of paternal leave.

sections.label: Security officers' working hours
sections.summary: The speaker raises the issue of security officers working 12 hours a day, six days a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, Madam, I would like to raise the issue of the unearthly working hours of security officers, who generally work 12 hours a day, six days a week.

sections.label: Work-life harmony for security officers
sections.summary: The speaker asks where work-life harmony is for the 50,000 security officers living this life now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Where is the work-life harmony for the 50,000 security officers who live this life right now?

sections.label: Government tenders security shifts
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to change security officer working hours in all Government tenders to eight to 10-hour shifts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask the Government, as one of the largest buyers of security services, to take the lead by changing the working hours for security officer in all Government tenders to eight to 10-hour shifts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This will have a knock-on effect on the shift durations for security officers in the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The chief issue in working conditions for security officers is that of unreasonable working hours.

sections.label: MOM legislation outsourced workers
sections.summary: The speaker calls on MOM to ensure upcoming legislation enshrining TAFEP guidelines includes obligations on buyers of outsourced services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To address this, I call on the MOM to ensure that the upcoming legislation enshrining the TAFEP guidelines includes obligations on buyers of outsourced services, in that, service agreements must not contain clauses that result in unfair or discriminatory working conditions for outsourced workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we fail to do this, Madam, we are leaving the employment conditions of almost 100,000 outsourced workers to be subject to the whims and fancies of service buyers and managing agents without recourse.

sections.label: Unitary PWM for professions
sections.summary: The speaker urges tripartite partners to adopt a unitary PWM for the same professions regardless of in-house or outsourced employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As regards the extension of the PWM to in-house cleaners, security officers, landscape workers, administrators and drivers, I would like to urge the tripartite partners to adopt a unitary PWM for the same professions, regardless of whether these workers are employed in-house or if they are outsourced workers.

sections.label: Economic growth and uncertainties
sections.summary: The speaker notes MTI's 3% to 5% growth projection for 2022 but remains mindful of pandemic and Ukraine war uncertainties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although I am heartened to hear that the MTI's projection of a 3% to 5% growth in Singapore's economy in 2022, I continue to be mindful of the uncertainties in the trajectory of the COVID-19 pandemic and the potential downside risks it has on our economy and our people, especially with also now the war in Ukraine.

sections.label: Ageing, diabetes, hypertension prevalence
sections.summary: Census shows residents aged 65 and above rose from 9% to 15.2%, while diabetes and hypertension crude prevalence also increased.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The 2020 population census report showed that residents aged 65 and above has increased from 9% to 15.2% over the last 10 years .

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Despite Singapore's effort to tackle diabetes, the crude prevalence of diabetes showed an increasing trend from 8.6 % in 2010 to 9.5% in 2019 to 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the numbers of patients with hypertension does not fare well either, with an increase of the overall crude prevalence of 24.2% in 2017 to 35.5% in 2019 to 2020.

sections.label: Young couples BTO housing difficulties
sections.summary: COVID-19 worsened home ownership challenges, with young couples struggling to ballot for BTO flats and the 'no flat, no child' idea prevalent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: COVID-19 has accentuated the challenges of home ownership amidst the supply crunch in the construction sector and the rising cost of utilities due to the increase in energy prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Many young couples in my constituency have written to me or approached me at Meet-the-People Sessions about their difficulties in successfully balloting for a Build-to-Order (BTO) flat although they want to settle down and have a family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In Singapore, a study conducted by the Asian Development Bank has shown that the idea of "no flat, no child" is prevalent among our young generation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This, in the face of our continued declining rate, is an important issue that I feel should be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There are two suggestions that I would like to suggest for better meeting the housing aspirations of young Singaporeans.

sections.label: Social workers' anxiety and depression
sections.summary: A study found nearly 60% of frontline social workers had anxiety and 45% had depression at the pandemic's height.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A study found that nearly 60% of frontline social workers were affected by anxiety at the height of the pandemic, with 45% facing depression.

sections.label: FSC caseloads during pandemic

sections.summary: For those aged between 55 and 64, that figure increases to $1,700 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For those aged between 55 and 64, that figure increases to $1,700 per month.

sections.label: Micro-loans for poorer individuals
sections.summary: A state-backed facility should be set up to provide micro-loans to poorer individuals to start microbusinesses such as home-based catering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A state-backed facility should be set up to provide micro-loans to poorer individuals to set up microbusinesses, such as home-based catering businesses, for example.

sections.label: Measuring social mobility and poverty
sections.summary: The passage calls for measuring intergenerational social mobility, establishing a poverty line, tracking child poverty and ComCare and rental reliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We need to invest in a rigorous measurement of intergenerational social mobility at least once every decade, a call I have made before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And a nationally recognised poverty line should be established, which could aid social workers in making decisions, a call made in this House by my colleague, then Non-Constituency Nominated Member Mr Yee Jenn Jong, in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We should also keep data on child poverty, which is key to intergenerational poverty and which many other countries do publish.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I propose that we track the intergenerational rate of reliance on ComCare Financial Assistance and rental housing.

sections.label: Workers' Party opposes Budget
sections.summary: Workers' Party MPs argued for policies helping the poor and vulnerable and cannot support the Budget over the 28% GST hike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this Budget debate, the Leader of the Opposition, Member of Parliament Ms He Ting Ru and other Workers' Party Members of Parliament have argued for other policies that will help the poor and the vulnerable, including why the Government's 28% GST hike is unhelpful and unnecessary, which is why the Workers' Party cannot support the Budget.

sections.label: COVID-19 support for self-employed
sections.summary: In Year One of COVID-19, almost 200,000 self-employed people were given $1,000 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Year One of COVID-19, almost 200,000 self-employed people were given $1,000 a month.

sections.label: Russian invasion of Ukraine
sections.summary: The Russian invasion of Ukraine is the largest conflict on the European continent since World War II.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Russian invasion of Ukraine is the largest conflict on the European continent since World War II.

sections.label: Defence spending is vital
sections.summary: Defence spending is vital and we must have the capability and resources to survive if war is visited on us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The first is that defence spending is vital and we must ensure we have the capability and resources to survive in the event war is visited on us.

sections.label: Ukraine war economic impact
sections.summary: Asks the Minister for Finance whether the Ukraine war causes significant economic turmoil and whether Budget measures are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Third – and this is more short term – I would also like to ask the Minister for Finance whether he sees any significant economic turmoil from the war in Ukraine on us and whether any additional measures may need to be taken in the Budget to provide for this.

sections.label: Easing restrictions, protecting vulnerable
sections.summary: Suggests easing restrictions toward normal life while reminding and educating the more vulnerable to take extra precautions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: My suggestion is that it may be better for us to proceed with plans to ease our restrictions and move closer to life as normal but, at the same time, remind and educate the more vulnerable to take extra precautions.

sections.label: Removing MOP for resale flats
sections.summary: Suggests HDB consider removing the MOP for resale flats while retaining it for new flats, disagreeing with MND's view.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: On the supply side, Build-to-Order (BTO) development has slowed down somewhat because of delays in construction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I had filed Parliamentary Questions on this previously and MND had indicated in its response that it did not believe removing MOP would increase housing supply and may encourage speculation because people who sell their flats may then look to buy new ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I do not agree with this view entirely and I would suggest, perhaps, initially, HDB may wish to consider removing the MOP for resale flats while retaining it for new flats.

sections.label: Resale and new flat price gap
sections.summary: States that a huge price discrepancy between resale flats and new flats is a big driver for new BTOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In my view, one of the biggest drivers for new BTOs is that there is a huge price discrepancy between resale flats and new flats.

sections.label: BTO and resale price disparity
sections.summary: Suggests a BTO flat price with resale levy be comparable to a resale flat to ease buyer choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think one of the reasons for the high demand for BTOs, in particular, is the disparity in prices between resale flats and BTO flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And I would suggest that, ideally, the price of a BTO flat with the resale levy should be somewhat comparable to a resale flat so that they become easy options for buyers to choose from.

sections.label: Wills fees, preschool GST costs
sections.summary: Suggests waiving the $50 wills registration fee, promoting MyLegacy, and exempting GST on preschool and after-school care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In conjunction with the talks covering estate planning, MinLaw can consider a further waiver of the $50 wills registration fees currently chargeable by the Singapore Academy of Law while encouraging inter-agencies to work closely together to promote the use of Smart Nation's MyLegacy portal for comprehensive estate planning services on matters, such as CPF nominations, advance medical directives, lasting power of attorney and wills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In terms of investing in our children, another area which I hope we can consider is to defray the costs of preschool and after-school care services, such as exempting the GST for these monthly expenses.

sections.label: Autistic children costs and 5Rs
sections.summary: Residents with autistic children say early intervention, speech therapy and childcare costs stretch middle-income families; the 5Rs are encouraged for the Green Plan 2030 goal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: During the course of my thematic e-townhalls which focus on embracing parenthood, as well as my regular house visits, several of my residents with autistic children have shared with me that, notwithstanding the fact that they belonged to the middle-income group, they find themselves financially stretched due to the costs incurred for signing up their children into the early intervention programmes and speech therapy sessions, coupled with the expenses incurred by them every month for enrolling their children in a kindergarten or childcare centre.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Lastly, we can further reduce our collective upkeep and progress towards our Singapore Green Plan 2030 goal by encouraging Singaporeans to practise not just the 3Rs but the full 5Rs: (a) reduce consumption of resources unless necessary; (b) reduce consumption of resources, such as water, electricity and food; (c) repair reparable items, such as electrical and electronic appliances; (d) reuse used items for different purposes, such as using reusable bags, bottles or food containers; and (e) segregate recyclable items and place them into recycling bins.

sections.label: GST increase delayed, support measures
sections.summary: The Government delayed the GST increase and continues support like S&CC rebates and GST vouchers to help Singaporeans cope with inflation, citing $100 CDC vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   In this Budget, the Government has listened to the voices of the people and delayed the increase in GST.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Continuing support, such as S&CC rebates, GST vouchers, will continue to help Singaporeans cope with rising cost of living due to inflation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Take, for example, the $100 CDC vouchers previously given out by the Government to each household.

sections.label: Financial planning guidance for life stages
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will provide professional financial planning guidance to Singaporeans before life stages such as starting a family, career, birth, ageing, sickness and death.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Starting a family, making a career, birth, ageing, sickness and death will definitely impose a heavy burden on us in different stages of our lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Hence, I hope that the Government will provide professional guidance to Singaporeans in financial planning before they enter these stages.

sections.label: GST increase staged, support schemes
sections.summary: The speaker understands the GST increase and commends its two-stage implementation in 2023 and 2024, and notes schemes like the Assurance Package, GST Voucher, U-Save and MediSave top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As such, I do understand the rationale behind the GST increase and commend the Government for being sensitive in implementing the GST increase in two stages, in 2023 and 2024, so that the immediate impact of the increase is not felt and this will give everyone, both consumers and companies, time to prepare for the hike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To further soften the blow of the increase and to help Singaporean households cope with the increase in the cost of living, I am also heartened to see that the Government has rolled out many other schemes, such as the enhanced Assurance Package with additional CDC vouchers and cash payout to eligible Singaporeans; enhanced permanent GST Voucher scheme; U-Save rebates; MediSave top-ups; and the addition of S&CC into the GSTV scheme.

sections.label: Progressive taxes beyond GST
sections.summary: The speaker says a holistic taxation strategy is important and commends the Government for exploring progressive taxes, including higher personal income tax above $500,000 and higher property tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As I have mentioned before, it is important to have a holistic taxation strategy and it is commendable that the Government is looking beyond GST as a revenue source and is also exploring other alternative sources of taxation revenue via other forms of progressive taxes, such as the increase in personal income tax for those with an annual income of more than $500,000 and an increase in property tax for non-owner-occupied property and owner-occupied property with an annual value of more than $30,000.

sections.label: Healthcare spending and mental wellness
sections.summary: The speaker is glad about increased healthcare spending and especially happy that the Government is focusing on mental wellness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: That is what I think we all should be aiming for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am personally glad to hear that there will be an increase in healthcare spending, and a specific area of healthcare that I am especially happy that the Government is focusing on is mental wellness.

sections.label: Men's mental health help
sections.summary: Ms Poh says men often mistake depression symptoms for physical issues and use negative coping like alcoholism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One of the nominees for Singaporean of the Year in 2021, Ms Poh has done a lot to help those with mental illness in my Ang Mo Kio-Hougang constituency and she shares these strong views that more needs to be done for men's mental health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I had a chat with Ms Poh lately and, according to her, men often tend to equate psychosomatic symptoms, such as racing heart, digestive issues or headaches, as health issues and seek help from physicians without realising that these are common symptoms of depression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: More worryingly, when depressed, men are more likely to engage in negative coping techniques, such as alcoholism, which may, ironically, lead to other forms of health problems in the long run. "During our sessions," says Ms Poh, "some male clients asked if it is okay for them to cry.

sections.label: Schools teaching male students
sections.summary: It asks whether schools or tertiary institutions could develop resources to teach male students to dispel toxic masculine stereotypes and speak up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Could our Secondary schools or tertiary institutions not develop dedicated resources and platforms to teach male students how to dispel traditionally toxic masculine stereotypes and encourage them to step forward and feel comfortable to speak up about their struggles and seek help?

sections.label: Social compact in Budget
sections.summary: It states that the heart of good governance is a strong social compact, reflected in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The heart of good governance is about creating a strong social compact, and the social compact is constantly evolving as our society progresses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And a key feature of our social compact is reflected in this Budget, which signals that those of us who are blessed to have more should contribute more, and those of us who need more help should get the help that they need.

sections.label: Situation escalated after invasion
sections.summary: It states that the situation has escalated sharply following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Since then, we all know that the situation has escalated sharply, following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

sections.label: Extending TRECS to SMEs
sections.summary: It cites extending the Temporary Electricity Contracting Support Scheme to help affected consumers, especially SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, extending the Temporary Electricity Contracting Support Scheme (TRECS) to help affected consumers, especially the SMEs.

sections.label: Budget support packages and GST
sections.summary: It states this Budget introduced the Jobs and Business Support Package and Household Support Package, with staggered tax moves and GST offsets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In this Budget, we introduced the Jobs and Business Support Package to help businesses and workers, as well as the Household Support Package to help households with their daily needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are staggering the tax moves, with the first step of the GST increase taking effect only next year and with generous offsets for all Singaporean households.

sections.label: EDP Renewables Singapore clean energy hub
sections.summary: EDP Renewables announced plans to invest up to $10 billion through Sunseap to establish a clean energy hub in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, after the Budget, Members may have read that EDP Renewables, a global leader in the renewable energy space, announced plans to invest up to $10 billion through a local firm Sunseap to establish a clean energy hub in Singapore for the Asia Pacific region.

sections.label: Budget payouts to SMEs
sections.summary: In this Budget, 80% of payouts from new and enhanced schemes will flow to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In this Budget, 80% of the payouts from the new and enhanced schemes will flow to SMEs.

sections.label: Government support for productivity projects
sections.summary: For a $10,000 productivity project, the Government will pay up to $7,000, and SMEs pay as little as $300.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For a $10,000 productivity project, the Government will pay up to $7,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If you do so, SMEs only need to pay as little as $300 for a $10,000 productivity project.

sections.label: Bringing back workers as borders open
sections.summary: As borders progressively open, priority is given to bringing back workers businesses urgently need, especially construction, marine and process sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As we progressively open our borders, we are giving priority to bringing back workers that businesses urgently need, especially workers for the construction, marine and process sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We should be able to clear the shortages within the next few months.

sections.label: Support for promising businesses to scale up
sections.summary: The Singapore Global Enterprises initiative will provide customised support to help promising businesses scale up and access capital, talent and networks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It even launched a food accelerator recently to help startups commercialise food technology, scale up and access new markets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We now have about 800 local enterprises with annual revenues above $100 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Through the new Singapore Global Enterprises initiative, we will provide customised support to help promising businesses scale up and better access the three areas of capital, talent and networks that Ms Janet Ang had mentioned so eloquently in her speech.

sections.label: Foreign workforce inflow and complementarity
sections.summary: Budget moves help ensure incoming workers are of the right calibre and strengthen complementarity of local and foreign workforce, but Singapore is not closing itself to foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The latest moves we have made in this Budget will help to ensure that the workers coming in are of the right calibre and in areas where we need them and further strengthen the complementarity of our local and foreign workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But I want to be very clear about one thing: we are not closing ourselves to the inflow of foreign workers and professionals.

sections.label: Budget cut savings reallocated
sections.summary: Savings from the planned 1% budget cuts are reallocated towards new priorities for new initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Ms Hazel Poa asked about the effect of the planned 1% budget cuts – let me clarify that the savings from these budget cuts are reallocated towards new priorities, because the Government is always seeking to embark on new initiatives for the benefit of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Growth of elderly aged 90
sections.summary: Those aged 90 and above rose from about 10,000 in 2010 to 22,000 now, and 700 rose to around 1,500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In 2010, we had about 10,000, aged 90 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Now, they have more than doubled to 22,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In 2010, we had 700; now, around 1,500.

sections.label: Government expenditure share of GDP
sections.summary: Over the last decade, Government expenditures rose from 15% to 18% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Over the last decade, Government expenditures rose from 15% to 18% of GDP.

sections.label: Temasek framework and raising taxes
sections.summary: Including Temasek in the framework followed a debate, and rules should not change to avoid raising taxes for recurring expenditure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That was to include Temasek into the framework and this was done after a robust and thorough debate in this House.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We should not, at the first sign of need, push for changes in the rules, just to take the easy way out and to avoid having to raise taxes to meet our growing recurring expenditure needs.

sections.label: Reserves, economy and NIRC
sections.summary: Reserves are growing but the economy, challenges and needs grow faster, and NIRC provided about 3.5% of GDP on average.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our reserves are growing, but the size of our economy, the challenges we face and the complexity of needs are growing even faster.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I have already explained that the NIRC has provided about 3.5% of GDP to the annual Budget, on average, in the last five years.

sections.label: Drawing on Past Reserves
sections.summary: Reserves risks are tilted downside, about $37 billion in Past Reserves was drawn over two years, and balanced Budget is committed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Members need to understand that the risks for our reserves are tilted on the downside.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have already drawn about $37 billion in Past Reserves over the past two years and are continuing to draw on them this year to keep up our public health defences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: While we are in a better position now, but we are not out of the woods yet.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And, I would say, we will not be able to put back what we have drawn down from the Past Reserves anytime soon.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Ms Foo Mee Har also asked whether we would be able to get back to a balanced Budget position.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are, certainly, committed to doing so, as we exit the crisis.

sections.label: NIRC and GST trade-off
sections.summary: Drawing more NIRC now means the next generation pays more taxes, as 20% less NIRC would raise GST to 11%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To illustrate, if we were to have just 20% less NIRC than today's levels – which could easily have happened if our predecessors had focused on their own spending and did not think it necessary to have a carefully designed Reserves Protection Framework – our GST would now need to increase to 11% instead of 9%, to make up for the funding gap.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, drawing more NIRC now means that our children and the next generation will end up paying more taxes.

sections.label: Mix of three tax types
sections.summary: Consumption taxes cannot be ignored; a good mix of income-based, asset-based and consumption-based taxes is needed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The short answer is we cannot just ignore consumption taxes and put the entire burden on income and wealth taxes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We need a good mix of all three types of taxes: income-based, asset-based and consumption-based.

sections.label: METR revenue uncertainty
sections.summary: It is hard to estimate with confidence how much more net tax revenue Pillars 1 and 2 can collect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In other words, if we have the same volume of investments and business activities in Singapore, even as taxes go up with the METR, yes, we will collect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is hard to estimate with any confidence whether or how much more net tax revenue we can collect from both Pillars 1 and 2.

sections.label: Tax incentives for small economies
sections.summary: Smaller economies could hitherto rely on tax incentives to make up for inherent disadvantages like limited land and labour force.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Hitherto, smaller economies like us could rely on tax incentives, not just non-tax factors, to make up for our inherent disadvantages, like limited land and labour force.

sections.label: GST versus PIT rate
sections.summary: Keeping GST at 7% and raising the same revenue through PIT would raise the top marginal rate from 22% to 42%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If we were to keep the GST at 7% and raise the same amount of revenue through PIT, the top marginal rate would have to go up from 22% to 42%.

sections.label: Property tax moves revenue
sections.summary: Property tax moves raise $380 million more per year from a base of 7% of owner-occupied and non-owner-occupied residential properties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
