sections.summary: Budget 2022's Progressive Wage Credit Scheme co-funds wage increases for lower-wage workers, and Workfare Income Supplement boosts workers' take-home earnings without discouraging work.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From that perspective, the use of wage subsidies or wage credits extended to firms as in the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS) announced in Budget 2022 to co-fund wage increases for certain lower-wage workers, as well as the wage income supplements extended to workers through the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) Scheme boost workers' take-home wage earnings without discouraging work.

sections.label: CPF rates and SINGA
sections.summary: Budget 2022 increases employer and employee CPF contribution rates of workers aged 55 to 70, boosting retirement adequacy; inter-generational distributive justice underpins SINGA.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even as the share of the ageing population increases and life expectancy rises, I note that Budget 2022, in increasing the employer and employee CPF contribution rates of workers aged 55 to 70, will boost their retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Inter-generational distributive justice provides a basis for the Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act (SINGA) passed in Parliament last year.

sections.label: Social surplus and GST burden
sections.summary: Society enables social collaboration creating social surplus used through the fiscal system; middle class Singaporeans bear an additional $1.2 billion yearly GST burden.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A society enables that social collaboration so that we create this social surplus.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And that social surplus can be utilised through the fiscal system to leave everyone better off than if we had each functioned in isolation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Middle class Singaporeans will have to bear an additional GST burden of $1.2 billion per year.

sections.label: EP levy versus GST hike
sections.summary: A monthly $1,200 EP levy would raise almost $3 billion and make the GST hike unnecessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If we impose a monthly $1,200 EP levy, as I had recommended in the Budget debate last year, and then again in the Foreign Talent and Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA) debate, the levy will raise almost $3 billion and make the GST hike unnecessary.

sections.label: Government financial assets reported
sections.summary: The Government reported $1.4 trillion of financial assets as of 31 March 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government reported $1.4 trillion of financial assets as of 31 March 2021.

sections.label: Land sales proceeds and unutilised revenue
sections.summary: Another $10 billion of annual land sales proceeds goes into reserves directly, giving $30 billion of unutilised revenue annually for future current year spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Another $10 billion of annual land sales proceeds is put into the reserves directly and not used for the current year spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thus, even without touching the growing reserves, we have a total of $30 billion of unutilised revenue annually, which can be deployed for the current year spending in the future.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme questions
sections.summary: Many Singaporeans questioned why the $30 billion Jobs Support Scheme supports profitable companies without a claw back feature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For the COVID-19 spending, many Singaporeans have questioned why the $30 billion Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) is used to support profitable companies without a claw back feature.

sections.label: GST increase and tax burden
sections.summary: Increasing GST adds $1.2 billion tax burden onto middle-class Singaporeans yearly, while income and wealth tax increases for the rich rise by less than $600 million yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: By increasing the GST, the Government will add $1.2 billion tax burden onto middle-class Singaporeans a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, income tax and wealth tax increases for the rich are expected to increase by less than $600 million a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: At the moment, we have at least $1.6 trillion reserves and $30 billion unutilised annual revenues.

sections.label: GST revenue calculation method
sections.summary: The data came from calculating the Minister for Finance's ratio of GST paid by top 20% and bottom 80%, giving $1.2 billion from 40% of $3 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Speaker, I got the data by calculating from the ratio given by the Minister for Finance in terms of the share of the GST paid by the top 20% and the bottom 80%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: If the total amount of GST revenue to be raised from a two-percentage point increase in GST, will be about $3 billion, so, 40% of $3 billion, I got my $1.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Can I ask Mr Leong whether he can confirm that his calculations do not take into account the amounts that middle-income residents of Singapore will receive under the Assurance Package and the permanent GSTV scheme?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Speaker, yes, the calculations do not take that into consideration.

sections.label: MAS inflation projection
sections.summary: MAS is projecting a 2% to 3% increase in prices this year, led by rising energy prices, supply bottlenecks and global demand recovery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: MAS is projecting a 2% to 3% increase in prices this year, led in part by rising energy prices due to geopolitical tensions, continuing supply bottlenecks and a recovery in global demand.

sections.label: GST increase and Assurance Package
sections.summary: Speaker thanks the Minister for Finance for delaying and staggering the GST increase and topping up the Assurance Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to thank the Minister for Finance for pushing back the start date and also staggering the GST increase across 2023 and 2024, as well as topping up the $6 billion Assurance Package that was announced in 2020, where the distribution of cash, rebates and vouchers will help households to offset five to 10 years of additional GST expenses.

sections.label: Median gross monthly income growth
sections.summary: After inflation adjustment, median gross monthly income rose 2.1% yearly from 2016 to 2021, down from 3.1% in 2011 to 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: After adjusting for inflation, the median gross monthly income has only increased 2.1% year-on-year between 2016 and 2021, down from 3.1% in the 2011 to 2016 period.

sections.label: Minimum qualifying salary for foreigners
sections.summary: Speaker welcomes the raising of the minimum qualifying salary for foreigners on Employment Passes or S Passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Second, I also welcome the raising of the minimum qualifying salary for foreigners to work in Singapore on Employment Passes (EP) or S Passes.

sections.label: Current-year pay-as-you-earn income tax
sections.summary: Speaker suggests relooking at assessing personal income tax on a current-year, pay-as-you-earn basis given income volatility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Fourth, given the context of an economy in transition, individuals may experience volatility in income levels or in employment altogether.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: It may be useful to relook at the option of assessing personal income tax on a current-year, pay-as-you-earn basis.

sections.label: MOM template for self-employed persons
sections.summary: Speaker asks if MOM can augment its key terms of engagement form template for self-employed persons with default contractual wording.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Is it possible for MOM to augment its "key terms of engagement form template for self-employed persons", to provide default contractual wording which freelancers can rely on to be the market standard and which they can rely on if the matter goes to the Court or the Small Claims Tribunal?

sections.label: Repeal of estate duty
sections.summary: Speaker asks if the 2008 decision to repeal estate duty, also known as inheritance tax, is being rethought.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: These progressive measures will ensure that "those with more will contribute more", while "those with less will still contribute, but a lesser amount, and they will receive more benefits in return".

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: But on the Minister's point that there is some difficulty in valuing and taxing wealth accurately, may I ask if we are rethinking our 2008 decision to repeal estate duty, also known as inheritance tax?

sections.label: Corporate tax competitiveness investment
sections.summary: The passage asks what the Government plans to do to preserve Singapore's attractiveness as an investment destination given erosion of corporate tax competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: What are the Government's plans to preserve Singapore's attractiveness as an investment destination in view of this erosion of our corporate tax competitiveness?

sections.label: Assurance Package GST coverage
sections.summary: The passage states that Finance Ministers explained the Assurance Package covers most Singaporeans for five years of GST increase and lower-income for at least 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister Heng also highlighted this two years ago in his 2020 Budget debate response speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Also, all the Finance Ministers have explained that the Assurance Package will cover the majority of Singaporeans for five years' worth of GST increase and the lower-income for at least 10 years' worth.

sections.label: Assurance Package payout examples
sections.summary: The passage gives examples of payments and rebates under the enhanced $6.6 billion Assurance Package offsetting GST increases for different households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Even though they would have to pay $806 in additional GST per year with the GST increase, they could receive payments and rebates of $3,850 over five years under the enhanced $6.6 billion Assurance Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: A three-generation family with two school-going children living in a 5-room flat could receive $6,740 over five years, offsetting about seven years of GST increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: In another example, a lower-income couple with two young children, who live in a 3-room HDB flat and earn a household income of $2,300 stands to receive $5,010 of payments and rebates offsetting about 12 years in GST increase!

sections.label: Cities of Tomorrow R&D programme
sections.summary: The passage states the Cities of Tomorrow R&D programme is an MND-led multi-agency effort with research focus areas addressing sustainability goals.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Cities of Tomorrow R&D programme is a multi-agency effort led by MND, to identify challenges that cities face and to develop solutions to address these challenges.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This programme has several research focus areas that address our sustainability goals.

sections.label: Retraining adult learners Singapore
sections.summary: The passage states Minister Chan Chun Sing highlighted the need to retrain about half a million adult learners yearly through continuing education and training programmes.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: During the Straits Times Education Forum 2022 held in February this year, Minister Chan Chun Sing highlighted the need for Singapore to retrain about half a million adult learners each year, through continuing education and training programmes.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As Minister Chan noted, and I quote, "The skills to learn fast, unlearn and relearn, become more important than getting a particular grade at a particular point in life".

sections.label: Sustainability courses at institutions
sections.summary: The passage lists sustainability-related courses offered by Ngee Ann Polytechnic, Temasek Polytechnic, SMU and NUS.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, Ngee Ann Polytechnic offers a specialist diploma in "Sustainable Facilities Management"; Temasek Polytechnic offers a diploma in "Energy Management and Sustainable Design"; SMU offers an executive education programme on "Sustainability and Sustainable Businesses"; and NUS offers a Master of Science programme on "Sustainable and Green Finance", just to name a few.

sections.label: International carbon credits offset
sections.summary: From 2024, carbon tax liable businesses may use international carbon credits to offset up to 5% of taxable emissions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From 2024, carbon tax liable businesses will be allowed to use international carbon credits to offset up to 5% of their taxable carbon emissions.

sections.label: Nature-based carbon offsets demand
sections.summary: This creates demand for high quality nature-based carbon offsets supporting forest conservation and reforestation internationally, aligned with Singapore's hub ambition.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Crucially, this will also create demand for high quality nature-based carbon offsets, to help support forest conservation and reforestation projects internationally.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These green transition measures are well aligned with Singapore's ambition to be a Global Carbon Services and Trading Hub.

sections.label: Post-Omicron return to industries
sections.summary: Experts forecast relative stability this year, so it is time to consider how Singaporeans in COVID-19 management return to their industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And once we get pass Omicron, experts globally have forecast a period of relative stability for this year, compared to the challenging last two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is time for us to start considering how to best encourage Singaporeans involved in COVID-19 management to go back to their industries.

sections.label: Manpower cost and inflation
sections.summary: Inflation is largely due to global supply bottlenecks and energy costs, but returning Singaporeans to industries helps companies manage manpower cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Of course, a large part of this inflation we see is largely due to global supply bottlenecks, as well as surging energy costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: But getting a number of Singaporeans currently involved in COVID-19 management back to the industries will certainly help our companies better manage manpower cost, thereby mitigating the rising cost of living.

sections.label: Non-Singaporeans supplement COVID-19 team
sections.summary: Non-Singaporeans from neighbouring countries can supplement the team using work passes or S Pass with clear sunset clauses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: We can also supplement this core team with non-Singaporeans from neighbouring countries, much like how non-Singaporeans serve as Auxiliary Police Officers (APOs) in some situations to supplement our Singapore Police Force (SPF) officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And the non-Singaporeans involved in COVID-19 management can be brought in using additional work pass or S Pass, but with clear sunset clauses that their permits are tied to whether or not there is a continued need for COVID-19 management.

sections.label: Review of SMMs after Omicron
sections.summary: Ministers indicated a thorough review of SMMs after the Omicron wave subsides, with a list of no-go activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Recently, our Minister for Finance and other MTF Ministers have indicated that they will do a thorough review of SMMs after the Omicron wave subsides.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I hope our MTF can come up with a carefully considered list of "no-go" activities and settings, but allow everything else to proceed.

sections.label: Steps before GST implementation
sections.summary: The Government took other steps before implementing the GST, including bonds, transferring MAS reserves to GIC, wealth tax and income tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Some careful observers are also heartened to see that the Government took a number of other steps first before implementing the GST which affects many Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: These steps include: one, financing long-term lumpy infrastructure projects through bonds; two, transferring a sizeable amount of MAS foreign reserves to GIC, so that we can generate more future income through our reserves; three, implementing wealth tax in a measured and practical way; and four, getting the very successful to contribute their fair share of income tax.

sections.label: Impact on economy and firms
sections.summary: The initial assessment is that the immediate and direct impact on the economy and firms has been manageable for now.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Our initial assessment is that the immediate and direct impact on our economy and firms has been manageable for now.

sections.label: Sanctions on Russia
sections.summary: Minister Vivian Balakrishnan announced that Singapore will act with like-minded countries to impose sanctions and restrictions on Russia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Earlier today, Minister Vivian Balakrishnan announced that we will act in concert with like-minded countries to impose appropriate sanctions and restrictions on Russia.

sections.label: LNG price increase
sections.summary: Liquefied natural gas prices have doubled from about $17 per MMBTU around half a year ago to about $35 currently.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, liquefied natural gas (LNG) prices have doubled from about $17 dollars per one million British Thermal Units (MMBTU), around half a year ago to about $35 currently.

sections.label: GDP and inflation projections
sections.summary: Singapore earlier projected GDP growth of 3% to 5% this year, with CPI all items inflation between 2.4% and 3.5% and MAS core inflation between 2% and 3%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: So, what does this mean for Singapore's economy?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We earlier projected our GDP would grow by 3% to 5% this year with CPI all items inflation ranging between 2.4% and 3.5% and the MAS core inflation between 2% and 3%.

sections.label: Real median income growth
sections.summary: Despite higher inflation, real median income of full-time employed residents grew close to 1% in 2021, and 4.4% for lower-income residents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Despite inflation having gone up, the real median income of full-time employed residents for 2021 grew by close to 1% in a COVID-19 year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The growth was significantly higher at 4.4% for lower-income residents at the lowest 20th percentile.

sections.label: Small Business Recovery Grant
sections.summary: The Small Business Recovery Grant gives $1,000 per local employee, capped at $10,000 per firm, to eligible firms in sectors most badly affected by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Small Business Recovery Grant (SBRG) of $1,000 per local employee up to a cap of $10,000 per firm will help eligible firms in sectors most badly affected by COVID-19.

sections.label: Additional CDC Vouchers
sections.summary: All Singaporean households will receive an additional $100 in Community Development Council Vouchers to help with daily expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: All Singaporean households will receive an additional $100 in Community Development Council Vouchers to help them with their daily expenses.

sections.label: Business transformation and worker upgrading
sections.summary: Resource-intensive firms must transform, workers must learn and upgrade, and a vibrant, diversified, resilient economy and cohesive society are needed to weather external shocks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Firms that are resource-intensive must recognise the need to transform their businesses and workforce, so that they are able to do more with less and unlock new business opportunities and access new markets and customers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Workers must also recognise that the best way for them to compete and stay employable in an increasingly volatile environment is to constantly learn and upgrade themselves, so that they remain relevant and productive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: I will share more about the challenges and economic opportunities that we see and how we will help businesses and workers overcome the challenges and capture these opportunities during the Committee of Supply debate on MTI later this week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: It is crucial that we strengthen our defences against such external shocks and to do that, we need to build a vibrant, diversified and resilient economy as well as forge a cohesive and united society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: While there are significant challenges ahead, I am confident that we can weather these headwinds if we work together – the people, the businesses and the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We have fared collectively well so far and I attribute this to the leadership of our Government, in the trust and cooperation of our citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I applaud the Government for boldly putting forward a holistic and expansionary Budget of $102.4 billion.

sections.label: Support for SMEs
sections.summary: The Progressive Wage Model and tighter foreign labour policies raise SME expenses, so the $500 million Jobs and Business Support Package and Budget 2022 measures are welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Locally, the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) and tighter foreign labour policies instituted will help uplift lower-wage workers and boost the hiring of residents respectively, but they translate to even greater expenses for our SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I, therefore, welcome the $500 million Jobs and Business Support Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Budget 2022 is clear in its push for SMEs to strengthen its capabilities: $200 million for digitisation schemes, $600 million to expand the Productivity Solutions Grant and $100 million to company skills training.

sections.label: MHA plan expenditure increase
sections.summary: Budget 2022 has provided for a modest 1.8% increase in MHA's plan expenditure, including keeping the country safe and secure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This includes keeping our country safe and secure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that Budget 2022 has provided for modest 1.8% increase in MHA's plan expenditure.

sections.label: Scams and victim losses
sections.summary: While physical crimes have plunged, scams quadrupled from 2017 and victims lost over $633 billion last year, more than the Jobs and Business Support Package or Households Support Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While physical crimes have plunged, scams quadrupled from 2017 and victims lost over $633 billion last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is more than the $500 million jobs in the Business Support Package or the $560 million Households Support Package (HSP) to help our young and old.

sections.label: Youths among new drug abusers
sections.summary: Youths aged 30 continue to form about 60% of new abusers in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding this, youths aged 30 continue to form about 60% of new abusers in recent years.

sections.label: Engaging youths against drugs
sections.summary: More could be done to engage youths, teachers and parents to deal with at-risk youths for timely intervention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We cannot allow the lives of youths, who are our future, to be marred by drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, more could be done in a concerted effort to engage youths and teachers at schools, as well as parents at home to deal with at-risk youths for timely intervention.

sections.label: Protection from profiteering
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will give more resources and power to consumer bodies to deal with profiteering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am convinced that people must be protected and have more effective recourse when they encounter profiteering situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Hence, I sincerely hope that the Government will continue to take cases of profiteering seriously and give more resources and power to the Consumers Association and the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore, as well as the soon-to-be-established Committee Against Profiteering, to deal with consumer complaints and effectively deal with unscrupulous businessmen who seek huge profits.

sections.label: NTUC job matching figures
sections.summary: NTUC's e2i helped match more than 46,000 workers to new or secondary jobs from February 2020 to December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As part of the NTUC Job Security Council (JSC), NTUC's e2i has helped match more than 46,000 workers to new or secondary jobs from February 2020 to December 2021.

sections.label: Higher property tax rates
sections.summary: Property tax rates for the portion of Annual Value above $30,000 will be raised from 4% to 16%, to 6% to 32%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The property tax rates for the portion of Annual Value in excess of $30,000, will be raised from 4% to 16%, to 6% to 32%.

sections.label: GSTV U-Save disbursement basis
sections.summary: The question asks whether GSTV U-Save rebates could be disbursed by per capita household income instead of HDB flat size.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Last but not least, regarding the additional GST Voucher (GSTV) – U-Save rebates under the Assurance Package and the regular GSTV – U-Save rebates, would the Government consider disbursing the rebates based on per capita household income instead of the size of the HDB flat?

sections.label: Top-tier tax rates and millionaires
sections.summary: Raising top-tier tax rates from 22% to 24% could collect an additional $170 million, as millionaires rose from 207,000 in 2019 to 270,000 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister has shared that by raising the top-tier tax rates from 22% to 24%, an additional $170 million of tax revenue could be collected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Over the past year, there has been a 30% increase in a number of millionaires in Singapore, from around 207,000 in 2019 to 270,000 in 2020.

sections.label: Low-wage workers and foreign labour
sections.summary: The speaker says slowing foreign labour supply will assist low-wage Singaporean workers, and is concerned businesses will pass cost increases to customers despite the PWCS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is no easy solution and we will need to assist our low-wage Singaporean workers by slowing the supply of foreign labour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I am concerned that even with the Government's Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS) to support part of the wage increases, businesses will still have to pass along some cost increases to customers and consumers.

sections.label: Retirees hit by rising costs
sections.summary: Retirees will be hit by the double impact of rising costs of living and the GST increase after next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Retirees will be hit by the double impact of the rising costs of living and the GST increase after next year.

sections.label: Diabetes prevalence and ethnic groups
sections.summary: Diabetes prevalence was 9.5% in 2019, up from 8.6% in 2016, and higher among Malays and Indians than Chinese.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, since then-Minister for Health Mr Gan Kim Yong declared "War on Diabetes" in 2016, the prevalence of diabetes is 9.5% in 2019, up from 8.6% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The prevalence of diabetes was higher among Malays and Indians at 14.4% and 14.2% respectively, compared to Chinese at 8.2%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider allocating more resources to customise health measures to help bring down the prevalence among the different ethnic groups?

sections.label: National Mental Health Competency Training Framework
sections.summary: The speaker enquires about the progress of the National Mental Health Competency Training Framework and says the Budget established a good framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: On this note, I would like to enquire from Minister for Health on the progress of the National Mental Health Competency Training Framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: All the more we need to take care of one another and leave no one behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We need to stay united to survive in a competitive global environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Budget has established a good framework for all of us to work together for our common future.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Credit Scheme support
sections.summary: The PWCS, introduced in Budget 2022, provides transitional wage support for employers adjusting to mandatory wage increases for lower-wage workers under the PWM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS), introduced in Budget 2022, provides transitional wage support for employers to adjust to upcoming mandatory wage increases for lower-wage workers covered by the Progressive Wage Model (PWM).

sections.label: Staggered GST increase for businesses
sections.summary: The decision to stagger the GST increase over two years is a strategic choice welcomed by businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The decision to stagger the increase of GST over the span of two years is another strategic choice welcomed by businesses.

sections.label: Foreign worker salary and productivity schemes
sections.summary: Calibrating EP and S Pass salaries encourages employers to consider foreign worker quality, while PSG and SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit raise productivity through digitalisation and skills upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By calibrating the minimum qualifying salary for Employment Pass (EP) and S Pass applicants, employers are strongly encouraged to further consider the quality of foreign workers that they want to bring in and how these workers also strengthen the larger workforce with our Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The second strategy aims to increase the productivity of our labour force through the digitalisation of processes and skills upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This strategy is materialised through schemes like the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) that subsidises the implementation of digital and automated solutions designed to raise productivity, and the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit that offsets up to 90% of expenses for skills upgrading initiatives.

sections.label: Early childhood ratios and manpower review
sections.summary: ECDA mandates early childhood teacher-student ratios, and the Government is asked to review essential services sectors' manpower requirements against local workforce numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: An example would be our early childhood sector where ECDA mandates a teacher to student ratio of one is to a range from eight to 25, depending on ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I seek the Government to review the essential services sectors' manpower requirements and the projected needs in the coming years vis-à-vis our local workforce numbers.

sections.label: Business mindset shift and short-term challenges
sections.summary: A radical business mindset shift is needed for global trends, but the Government is asked what else can address short-term challenges in building a resilient labour force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I acknowledge that a radical mindset shift on the part of businesses is needed to respond to larger global trends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, I would like to ask the Government, what else can be done to address the short-term challenges that businesses face in building a resilient labour force?

sections.label: SINGA borrowing and green bond funding
sections.summary: SINGA allows borrowing up to $90 billion for long-lasting infrastructure, and green bonds will fund public sector green projects, with questions on local business opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act (SINGA) will allow the Government to borrow up to $90 billion to pay for infrastructure that will last for at least 50 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To diversify the funding options for green infrastructure, Budget 2022 announced that $35 billion of green bonds will be issued by 2030 to fund public sector green infrastructure projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This builds on the $19 billion worth of green bonds issued during Budget 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In relation to these new sources of funding, I would like to ask the Government to provide more details on the infrastructural projects that have been earmarked for development and specifically the opportunities for our local businesses to be involved in these developments so that they can build necessary capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In addition to the other opportunities in the green economy, does the Government view engineering solutions in climate change adaption as a sector where our businesses can hone a niche in and eventually export solutions internationally?

sections.label: Singapore labour force and foreign talent
sections.summary: The Singaporean labour force is not big enough, and the Minister for Finance said Singapore remains open to global talent while focusing on complementarity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The reality is that the Singaporean labour force is not big enough.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, I am very glad to hear in Minister for Finance’s speech that we will remain "open and welcoming to talent from around the world but we will focus on complementarity".

sections.label: Refining progressive and wealth tax
sections.summary: The passage says social needs must be paid for and calls for refining the progressive and wealth tax regime while being careful of unintended consequences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And we also have, as the Minister for Finance pointed out, more and more social needs that have to be paid for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We can and should look into refining our progressive and wealth tax regime, with a caveat that we need to be careful of any unintended consequences.

sections.label: Separating growth from workforce care
sections.summary: The passage states that policies should separate the needs for growth from the need to care for the displaced workforce so growth potential is not unnecessarily limited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When crafting our policies, we should separate the needs for growth, from the need to care for the displaced workforce, so that we do not unnecessarily limit our growth potential.

sections.label: Lifting lower-wage workers, taxing top
sections.summary: The passage states lower-wage workers get a lift through Workfare and progressive wage subsidies, while top income brackets are taxed moderately and contribute 80% of personal income tax revenue.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Our lower-wage workers will be given a much desired lift through increased Government expenditures in Workfare and subsidies to help employers co-fund progressive wage increases.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Those in the top income brackets, while being asked to contribute more, are still only taxed moderately, as compared to many first-world countries.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is noteworthy that the top 10% of our income taxpayers contribute to 80% of personal income tax revenue.

sections.label: Gradual carbon tax increase
sections.summary: The passage states the carbon tax gradually rises to $50 per tonne and a further $80 per tonne by 2030, addressing the need to price in externalities.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the gradual increase in carbon tax to $50 per tonne and a further $80 per tonne by 2030, this starts to address the need to price in externalities and is a laudable move.

sections.label: Renewable diesel for emissions reduction
sections.summary: The passage states a transitional option could be reducing Scope 1 direct emissions using alternative fuels such as renewable diesel for land transport, logistics and construction sectors.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: One transitional option could be reducing our Scope 1 direct emissions via the use of alternative fuels, such as renewable diesel, also known as RD, which produces only one-tenth of conventional diesel's emissions, for the land transport, logistics and construction sectors.

sections.label: Carbon credits and IRECs regulation
sections.summary: The passage states international carbon credits can offset up to 5% of taxable emissions, and suggests Singapore consider regulating International Renewable Energy Certificates as an alternative for corporate compliance.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The ability to use international carbon credits to offset up to 5% of taxable emissions will support the development of a regulated carbon market in Singapore and the region.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I would also like to suggest that Singapore incorporate and consider regulating the use of International Renewable Energy Certificates, also known as IRECs, as an alternative means to carbon credits for corporate compliance in taxable emissions.

sections.label: Singapore REC prices and IRECs
sections.summary: Singapore REC prices doubled in a year from $35 to $70 per MWh, and regulating IRECs could add market liquidity and support net-zero developments.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Prices for Singapore RECs have doubled in the last one year, from $35 per megawatt hour (MWh) to $70 per MWh.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: By encouraging and regulating IRECs as an alternative environmental attribute next to carbon credits, this could provide greater liquidity in the market and also support major developers' pursuit of net-zero carbon developments.

sections.label: Sound Blaster cards success
sections.summary: A computer chipboard let users play and record speech and music, selling over 400 million Sound Blaster cards worldwide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is probably difficult to comprehend why the hype over quality music and sound over a desktop computer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: It was a computer chipboard that enabled users to play and record speech and music, selling more than 400 million Sound Blaster cards worldwide and the first Singapore company to be listed on NASDAQ.

sections.label: Singapore R&D spending 2017
sections.summary: According to the World Bank, Singapore's 2017 R&D spend was 1.94% of GDP, an estimated US$6.7 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: According to the World Bank, in 2017, Singapore's R&D percentage spend of GDP was 1.94% or an estimated US$6.7 billion.

sections.label: WIPO Singapore innovation rankings
sections.summary: From 2018 to 2020, WIPO ranked Singapore first in innovation inputs but 15th in innovation outputs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Looking further into the details of report from 2018 to 2020, WIPO ranked Singapore number one in innovation inputs but ranked 15th in innovation outputs.

sections.label: Singapore innovation output versus investment
sections.summary: Singapore produced less innovation outputs relative to its level of innovation investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Singapore produced less innovation outputs relative to its level of innovation investments.

sections.label: China AI research paper share
sections.summary: China's global share of research papers in one AI field rose from 4.26%, about 1,000 papers in 1997, to 27.68% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: China's global share of research papers in the few of just one AI has vaulted from 4.26%, which is about 1,000 papers in 1997, to 27.68% in 2017.

sections.label: Chinese AI firms count
sections.summary: As of March 2019, China had 1,189 AI firms, second to the US with over 2,000 active AI firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: As of March 2019, the number of Chinese AI firms has reached 1,189, second to only the US which has more than 2,000 active AI firms.

sections.label: Re-establishing Ministry of Science and Technology
sections.summary: It may be timely to consider re-establishing the Ministry of Science and Technology to focus Singapore's science, technology and innovation efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Given the emerging trends and existential nature of science and technology for Singapore's future, it may be timely to consider re-establishing the Ministry of Science and Technology to bring laser focus on making Singapore scientific, technology and innovation efforts more effective.

sections.label: Increasing R&D investment
sections.summary: Singapore should commit a larger percent of GDP to R&D, aiming for at least the OECD average of 2.4% and 3% to 4% in five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: One of the most important commitments is to increase the total R&D investment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Given Singapore's relatively small GDP, we must aim to commit a much larger percent GDP spent on R&D to sustain and keep up with the competition to achieve at least the OECD average of 2.4% today and with a further commitment to increase 3% to 4% of GDP in the next five years.

sections.label: Immigrant founders of US start-ups
sections.summary: The National Foundation for American Policy finds 55% of US billion-dollar start-ups have at least one immigrant founder, creating 1,200 jobs per company on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the United States, the National Foundation for American Policy finds that 55% of the billion-dollar start-up companies in the United States has at least one immigrant founder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Among privately held billion-dollar start-up companies in the United States, those with immigrant founders have created an average of 1,200 jobs per company in the US.

sections.label: OECD PhD and higher education percentages
sections.summary: According to the World Economic Forum, the OECD average for PhDs and higher education was 1.1%, with Israel, US, Switzerland, Germany, Sweden and Denmark leading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: According to World Economic Forum, percentage of PhDs and higher education OECD average was 1.1% with most innovative countries taking the lead, like Israel, US, Switzerland, Germany at 3%, 1.4% or 2%, Sweden and Denmark.

sections.label: Autism Resource Centre and Ensign Infosecurity collaboration
sections.summary: The speaker describes an 18-month journey where ARC and Ensign Infosecurity trained neo-diverse individuals and placed them in ICT and cybersecurity jobs with support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The last 18 months was the most rewarding journey for me, a journey that is proved to those who are new diverse and can hold good jobs that pay well and have rewarding careers, careers in ICT and cybersecurity, an industry with much promise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: I work closely with sister Denise Phua and a team in Autism Resource Centre (ARC), supportive bosses, Delan and Casey, my teammates Zaishao, Arian and Ken Hwee, with leading cybersecurity company Ensign Infosecurity, with the support of Tammy and Steven, it was an open collaborative environment, where ARC identified neo-diverse individuals and together with Ensign Infosecurity, trained them and emplaced them in high-quality jobs and provided them with job support.

sections.label: Cybersecurity analyst hiring increase
sections.summary: A pilot training programme of four cybersecurity analysts a year will increase hiring by 400% to four per quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: From a small training pilot programme of four cybersecurity analysts a year, within two months, and because of these individuals' remarkable performance, we will now want to increase hiring by 400% from four per year to four for every quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Be bold in investing in our people and there will be a place for all of us.

sections.label: Rising cost of living
sections.summary: With core inflation at 2.1% in December 2021 and the impending GST hike, the speaker raises cost of living for consideration.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: With core inflation having risen to 2.1% in December 2021, and with the impending hike of the GST, it is only natural that the cost of living continues to bear on the minds of our people.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: While I am thankful that the Government uses tax rebates, cash payouts and other forms of aid to cushion the impact of the GST hike for a large majority of Singaporeans, particularly the low-income group, I would like to raise the following for consideration towards a multi-prong approach to address the rising cost of living on the longer-term horizon.

sections.label: Redesigning supply chains and buffers
sections.summary: Singapore's scarcity of natural resources and reliance on imports make redesigning supply chains and buffers critical.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Singapore's scarcity of natural resources and heavy reliance on imports for necessities from food to energy, meant the impetus to redesign our supply chains and buffers to better weather the inflation due to shortages from time to time is critical.

sections.label: 30 by 30 food plan
sections.summary: The 30 by 30 plan focuses on supplying 30% of nutritional needs by 2030 but excludes food volume supply.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: The "30 by 30" plan today outlined the focus on the supply of 30% of our nutritional needs by 2030, but it does not include how we are looking at the food volume supply.

sections.label: Upskilling and supplemental income pathways
sections.summary: SkillsFuture and SGUnited support upskilling, but the speaker asks what supplemental pathways can provide additional income streams.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Over the years, much has been done to support the upskilling of workers through SkillsFuture and SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programmes.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, beyond that, what can be done to provide supplemental pathways to enable our workers to have additional income streams beyond their day job?

sections.label: Expanding micro jobs
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether micro jobs can be expanded for part-time workers, women with family care duties and senior workers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Could we consider how to expand the scale of micro jobs to fit the needs of part-time workers where women with family care duties and senior workers can also better participate in the workforce?

sections.label: Budget revenue strategies
sections.summary: Minister Lawrence Wong's recent Budget outlined new strategies for generating government revenues, mainly through progressive taxation on different income tiers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: The recent Budget by Minister Lawrence Wong outlined new strategies in generating government revenues, primarily through progressive taxation on different income tiers.

sections.label: Import reliance and inflation
sections.summary: Singapore's reliance on imports for resources means inflation and rising cost of living would be constant in the years ahead.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: To summarise, Sir, with Singapore's reliance on imports for resources, inflation and by extension, the rising cost of living would be a constant fixture in the years ahead.

sections.label: GST delay and assistance
sections.summary: The Government delayed and staggered GST, continues absorbing GST on essentials, and enhanced Workfare Income Supplement and GSTV schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the Government has listened to ground feedback.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It has not only delayed the GST implementation, but has staggered it over two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I have also previously asked whether additional assistance would be provided on top of the Assurance Package and the GST Voucher (GSTV) scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am pleased that the Government will continue to absorb GST on essentials like healthcare and education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Permanent schemes like the Workfare Income Supplement and the GSTV schemes are also enhanced.

sections.label: CPF rates for seniors
sections.summary: The passage applauds raising CPF contribution rates for senior workers to facilitate meaningful employment for seniors who wish to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One particular area is to facilitate meaningful employment for our seniors, who wish to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I applaud the raising of CPF contribution rates for senior workers.

sections.label: Caregiver service platform
sections.summary: The passage calls for a simple platform integrating all resources and service providers so caregivers can compare options and costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Having choices and a lack of clear information complicates matters for caregivers trying to find the most suitable and affordable formal care service for their family's needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We need a simple platform that integrates all available resources and service providers, for caregivers to seek out all the available options and do their own cost-benefit analysis.

sections.label: Palliative care training survey
sections.summary: A 2021 survey found only four in 10 healthcare professionals received training in palliative care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Only four in 10 of healthcare professionals received training in palliative care, according to a 2021 survey.

sections.label: Government palliative care funding
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will provide more resources and funding and how it will lead to improve palliative care quality and awareness in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Government provide more resources and funding to support this effort?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will the Government take the lead to improve the quality of palliative care and to generate more awareness in Singapore?
